item.title: Bayelsa boat mishap death toll rises to 32
item.description: •As Bayelsa deploys crane to lift wreckage of capsized boat •PANDEF mourns victims •Police AIG visits Ayama-Ijaw By Samuel Oyadongha & Henry Umoru The death toll in last Friday’s boat mishap in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 32, as the state government deployed a heavy-duty crane to the scene to lift the wreckage of the capsized vessel and facilitate a thorough search for persons who may still be trapped beneath or within it. This came as Pan Niger Delta Forum, PANDEF, the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone, mourned victims of the recent boat accident that claimed several lives. Also, the Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of Zone 16, Regina Udoette, has visited the Ayama-Ijaw waterside in Southern Ijaw to interact with marine workers and the Red Cross rescue team over the fatal boat mishap. The operation, involving the Bayelsa State Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, the Bayelsa State Emergency Management Agency, BYSEMA, the National Inland Waterways Authority, NIWA, security agencies, divers and other relevant responders, is continuing as the government intensifies efforts to account for all persons affected by the tragic incident. It was learned that the deployment of the crane was aimed at removing the submerged wreckage and enabling divers and rescue personnel to properly examine the site, while extending the search to areas that may not have been accessible during the initial operations. The state government had sustained the search and recovery effort since the mishap, with relevant agencies working to ensure that every part of the affected waterway and the wreckage was thoroughly examined. The latest deployment signals an escalation of the multi-agency operation, as authorities move to conclusively determine the fate of passengers who remain unaccounted for since the vessel went down. The boat tragedy, which occurred on the state’s inland waterways, around Oweikorogha and Otuan junction in the council, has once again brought to the fore concerns over water transportation safety in Bayelsa, a riverine state where boats serve as a primary means of movement for many communities. PANDEF mourns victims In a statement by PANDEF National Chairman, Amb. Godknows Igali, said: “PANDEF particularly commiserates with the affected families, the government and people of Bayelsa State, the people of Southern Ijaw council, and the affected communities, who have been impacted by this tragedy. We stand in full solidarity with them, share in their sorrow and extend the heartfelt condolences of the peoples of the entire South-South geopolitical zone. “While mourning this tragic loss, PANDEF calls on the relevant emergency relief agencies, security agencies and regulatory authorities to work closely with the Bayelsa State government to ensure that all necessary measures are taken to assuage the impact on survivors and bereaved families. “More importantly to take all necessary measur

item.title: Auburn Tigers flip top CB recruit from Bill Belichick, North Carolina
item.description: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Auburn Tigers flip top CB recruit from Bill Belichick, North Carolina appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Alex Golesh and the Auburn Tigers poached a solid prospect from Bill Belichick and the North Carolina Tar Heels, landing Nazir Pitchford to their future secondary. Pitchford announced his decision to commit to the Tigers on Monday, per On3 insider Hayes Fawcett. Hailing from Palmetto, Florida, he had been committed to the Tar Heels since June before changing course. Pitchford stands out as a three-star defender with an 86 score on 247Sports. He ranks 102nd among players in the state of Florida and 111th among players at his position. His composite score of 0.8644 puts him at 121st, 125th and 1,267th nationally in the 2027 class. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Pitchford explained his decision to join Auburn during an interview with On3. “My official visit to Auburn was a great experience,” Pitchford told Rivals. “The atmosphere, coaching staff, and overall environment really stood out to me. I enjoyed every moment and appreciate the Auburn family.” “Coach Banks has been recruiting me, and I really appreciate the relationship we’ve built. He’s been consistent with me, communicates well, and makes me feel like I’m a priority. I can tell he genuinely believes in me and what I can bring to the program.” What’s next for Auburn after landing Nazir Pitchford Alex Golesh and Auburn are showing off their recruiting chops. Getting Nazir Pitchford from North Carolina gives them a solid defender to utilize in the 2027 class. Auburn sits with a 7-4 overall record this season, going 4-4 in its SEC matchups so far. They sit at ninth place in the conference standings, being above the Missouri Tigers and the South Carolina Gamecocks while trailing the Ole Miss Rebels and the Kentucky Wildcats. The Tigers will look forward to their regular-season finale before gearing up for bowl game action. They take on the Alabama Crimson Tide in Week 13 as kickoff commences on Nov. 28 at 7:30 p.m. ET. item.title: Phoenix Suns extend winning streak with thrilling overtime victory over Pelicans
item.description: Dec 5, 2025; Houston, Texas, USA; Phoenix Suns guard Collin Gillespie (12) dribbles the ball during the fourth quarter against the Houston Rockets at Toyota Center. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images NEW ORLEANS — It wasn’t just another hard-fought victory; it was a character-building win for the Phoenix Suns. They are beginning to discover something important about themselves: they can win games even when things aren’t going according to plan. Phoenix escaped New Orleans with a 121-117 overtime win Monday night, extending its winning streak to four. However, the result required considerably more effort than expected against a struggling, shorthanded Pelicans team. Dec 27, 2025; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; Phoenix Suns guard Devin Booker (1) dribbles against New Orleans Pelicans guard/forward Micah Peavy (14) during the second half at Smoothie King Center. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images The Suns struggled to establish control on the defensive glass. New Orleans repeatedly created second-chance opportunities, turning missed shots into additional possessions and refusing to let Phoenix pull away. Devin Booker appeared ready to deliver the decisive moment late in regulation, connecting on a midrange jumper. But New Orleans answered again. Booker subsequently lost possession under pressure from Herb Jones on Phoenix’s final opportunity, sending the game into overtime after a desperation attempt at the buzzer fell short. Nov 10, 2025; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Phoenix Suns forward Dillon Brooks (3) against the New Orleans Pelicans in the second half at the Mortgage Matchup Center. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images That’s where the Suns showed another side of their developing identity. Collin Gillespie continued demonstrating why his composure matters in high-pressure situations. With Phoenix still searching for consistent answers at point guard, his ability to organize possessions and contribute when the game tightens becomes increasingly valuable. Jalen Green also brought a noticeable intensity, while Phoenix became more physical defensively. Booker even battled Zion Williamson for loose balls, illustrating a team that wasn’t willing to surrender another opportunity. Dec 26, 2025; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; Phoenix Suns forward Dillon Brooks (3) calls for a foul against New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson (1) during the first half at Smoothie King Center. Mandatory Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Rebounding remains an issue, and turnovers continue to create unnecessary problems. Those weaknesses could become considerably more damaging against stronger Western Conference opponents. But these are the types of games developing teams need to win. Phoenix didn’t dominate, and the opponent’s record and injury situation made this a favorable matchup on paper. Still, the Suns found a way. If Green maintains his aggression, Gillespie continues delivering in important moments, and Phoenix improves its rebounding,

item.title: How Luis Gil Will Impact Detroit Tigers
item.description: Sep 10, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees pitcher Luis Gil (81) delivers a pitch during the ninth inning against the Colorado Rockies at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor The Detroit Tigers signed free agent Luis Gil to a one-year deal with a $2.3 million base salary, plus up to $2 million in incentives. The New York Yankees released the 2024 AL Rookie of the Year at the non-tender deadline on Friday. Although the Bronx Bombers shifted Gil to the bullpen at the back end of last season, Tigers manager AJ Hinch will reportedly give the player a chance to make the rotation out of spring training. Here is how Gil will fit into the Tigers organization. Luis Gil Could Be Major Bargain for Detroit Tigers Detroit already looks to have a good amount of depth at starting pitcher. Framber Valdez still has two more seasons to go on his mammoth free agent contract , while the team recently extended the promising Troy Melton to a six-year deal . Barring injury, they should lock down the top two spots in the rotation. Competing for the remaining three spots are Gil, Keider Montero, River Ryan, Jackson Jobe, Drew Anderson, and Reese Olson. There will be room for a swing man in the bullpen, but there are still more arms than room on the roster. Apr 26, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; New York Yankees starting pitcher Luis Gil (81) delivers a pitch during the second inning against the Houston Astros at Daikin Park. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images The team has some flexibility within this group as to whether they start the season with the big club or with Triple-A Toledo. Jobe has all three minor league options left, while Olson and Ryan have two each. Meanwhile, Montero has just one option left , and both Gil and Anderson are out of minor league options. Olson missed the entirety of the 2026 season after he underwent right shoulder labrum repair surgery, so he would be a good bet to be assigned to Toledo to build himself up again. Assuming the team wants to carry a swingman, that still means that one pitcher will be left off the MLB roster. Out of the pitchers with options left, Ryan has the least experience at the major league level, while Jobe is the youngest, so likely one of the two will miss out. How Can Luis Gil Bounce Back Gil utilizes a four-pitch mix, throwing both a four-seam fastball and a sinker alongside a changeup used against lefties and a slider against righties. He has a less-than-stellar injury history, as he has one Tommy John surgery under his belt, plus major injuries in each of the last two seasons, which limited him to just under 85 innings pitched during that time. Since winning the Rookie of the Year award in 2024, Gil has also struggled with command and has seen his strikeout numbers go down while he has given up many more hits and home runs than in his only full major league season. item.title: Saints RB Travis Etienne Jr. gets honest about what’s holding him back amid return
item.description: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Saints RB Travis Etienne Jr. gets honest about what’s holding him back amid return appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . New Orleans Saints running back Travis Etienne first reappeared against the Carolina Panthers on Nov. 15 . But he hasn’t shown the past 1,000-yard potential that made him revered with the Jacksonville Jaguars. So what’s holding him back amid his return? Etienne became honest with reporters on Monday, saying it’s more of a mental thing. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “It’s more mental. […] Like yesterday, I feel like I definitely should have scored.” #Saints RB Travis Etienne Jr. on if he feels he’s back to full speed following his hamstring injury that landed him on injured reserve. pic.twitter.com/X3XG1ENXbH — NOF (@nofnetwork) November 23, 2026 Etienne has racked up just 218 yards on the ground. But he settled for just 14 yards on eight carries against the Panthers. The veteran RB showed flashes of his old self against the Chicago Bears , carrying the ball 14 times for 76 yards and averaged 5.4 yards a carry. New Orleans took two losses against both NFC foes, though. Now the Saints are watching their season fade in season two under coach Kellen Moore . New Orleans has fallen to 3-7 overall, and are facing its third consecutive double-digit losing season and fourth in the last five years. New Orleans hasn’t delivered three straight 10-loss or more campaigns since the late Mike Ditka led the franchise from 1997 to 1999. Meanwhile, the rival Panthers jumped two spots in front of the Saints and lead the division with a 5-5 record. The Saints happen to be in a logjam with the other NFC South teams, though. Everyone from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Atlanta Falcons and N.O. are 3-7 too. But it’s the Saints sitting at the bottom of the standings and are losers of two straight games. New Orleans won’t face an easy challenge on Sunday too, as the Saints will take on the AFC North leading Cincinnati Bengals on the road. item.title: Curfew in Delta: How gunmen killed 4 in Omo-Agege’s convoy
item.description: By Henry Umoru No fewer than four persons were killed, yesterday, as gunmen opened fire on members of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, who were on the campaign train of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, in Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. Omo-Agege is the Delta Central Senatorial candidate of the NDC in 2027 National Assembly polls. While the NDC claimed the All Progressives Congress, APC, was responsible for the attack, the ruling party accused the NDC of stoking the attack, which, it alleged, claimed three of its members. But the state police command said it was investigating the attack. Among NDC members killed was Moses Anaughe, a former Commissioner, Federal Character Commission and aide to Omo-Agege. A former member of the Delta State House of Assembly, Chief Evans Ivwurie, was among those shot and currently battling for his life alongside other victims receiving medical attention. Videos circulating on social media showed Umukoro, popularly known as Akhima, lying motionless at a hospital where efforts were being made to revive him. Another video showed Iwurie being assisted into a hospital, with blood stains visible around his chest. This came as the Delta State government imposed a curfew on Ughelli North, following the gunshots and attendant deaths in parts of the council. Meanwhile, Ughelli North Council Chairman, Olorogun Jaro Egbo, claimed that three of his supporters were killed, with both sides accusing the each other of instigating the violence. The State Police condemned the killings, and commenced investigations to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible. The latest bloodshed was the third major violent incident linked to political activities involving rival camps in the state, following earlier clashes in the Warri-Effurun axis and Asaba, where one person was killed. While Omo-Agege’s camp put the Uduere death toll at four, Egbo claimed three of his supporters were killed, with both sides accusing each other of instigating the violence. The recurrence of deadly confrontations, with the 2027 general elections still months away, has heightened concerns over the safety of political campaigns and the possibility of Delta becoming increasingly engulfed in political violence. Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation alleged that armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage at close range during a peaceful campaign visit, describing the incident as an assassination attempt. Assasination attempt In a statement by his Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, the campaign organisation said: “We condemn in the strongest possible terms the murderous attack on the campaign team of Senator Omo-Agege, Delta Central senatorial candidate of the NDC, in Uduere, Ughelli North. “According to eyewitness reports received from the scene, armed men opened fire at close range on Senator Omo-Agege and his entourage during a peaceful campaign tour to Uduere. “Sena

item.description: Cincinnati Bengals safety Bryan Cook (6) walks the sideline in the first quarter of the NFL International Week 9 game between the Atlanta Falcons and the Cincinnati Bengals at Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. The Bengals won the international matchup, 34-17. Bengals’ Bryan Cook gives fans a scare after apparent injury in MNF vs. Commanders appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach Zac Taylor ’s Cincinnati Bengals led Dan Quinn’s Washington Commanders 10-7 at halftime in Week 11 Monday Night Football action after receiver Tee Higgins unveiled a classy tribute before the game . Bengals QB Joe Burrow got MVP hype before the game, while the team’s Al Golden-led defense held Jayden Daniels’ offense to 107 yards in the first half. Golden’s unit’s defensive brilliance was tempered by an injury to safety Bryan Cook, whose status got an update . “Cook gets up and is walking off on his own power,” reporter Paul Dehner Jr. wrote on X. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Slight limp, but that’s a good sign considering how concerning the replay looked.” Cook landed at an awkward angle, appearing to writhe in pain before exiting the field. His injury drew concern from Commanders QB Jayden Daniels. Bryan Cook is able to walk off after this scary injury👏 Glad he's okay pic.twitter.com/2aYLK1LnQg — Chat Sports (@ChatSports) November 24, 2026 Cook had one tackle for Golden’s defense as the Bengals attempted to stymie the Daniels-led Commanders in Washington, D.C. The Bengals put up 188 first-half yards against the Commanders on offense, 167 of which came from its top-ranked passing offense as Burrow had 179 yards and a touchdown compared to 85 yards from Daniels who was sacked three times. Taylor had high praise for his offense heading into the big Monday Night Football clash, which the Bengals lived up to against a talented opponent on the road. Cook’s injury showed that nothing is guaranteed in the National Football League as one awkward play can bring an otherwise strong and healthy player to his knees, and force him to rely on the training staff for help. The Bengals continued to chase a big win in Washington, D.C. as they thanked their lucky stars the Cook injury wasn’t as bad or worse than it originally looked. item.title: Everything Dan Lanning said before Oregon hosts Washington
item.description: The Oregon Ducks have come a long way during their four-game winning streak. From seemingly impossible playoff odds to having the inside track to the Big Ten title game, everything is at stake this Saturday night in the regular-season finale against the Washington Huskies . The Ducks picked up a big win at Michigan State on a short week and head into the final game of the season at Autzen Stadium with the potential to win their way into the conference championship game and secure a spot in the College Football Playoff. Dan Lanning didn't waste time shifting focus to Washington, as it's a rivalry game Oregon never takes lightly. Washington knocked off Indiana in overtime last week in Seattle, clearing a path for Oregon to reach Indianapolis and the Big Ten Championship Game . The Huskies , not unlike the Ducks, have hit their stride on offense in recent weeks and have some momentum heading into Eugene. Lanning detailed his thoughts on the upcoming matchup, as well as the status of several key injuries and Oregon's conference title and playoff hopes heading into Senior Day at Autzen Stadium. Here's everything Lanning had to say at his weekly press conference on Monday night before Oregon hosts Washington. Opening Statement Dan Lanning: "Obviously an exciting opportunity for us this weekend. Get an opportunity to play a rival and our seniors' last game here potentially in Autzen. So exciting for them, especially for the guys that have given so much to this program and been involved for as long as they have. And for it to be a game like this one is a special opportunity for us. Washington's coming off a big win against Indiana and played extremely well, had as many yards as anybody has against that team this year, and it seems like things are really clicking for them. So I think both of us are on the uptick, and they've been as good as anybody. This season on the road, and certainly in the fourth quarter, they've gotten better and better. So, a really good opportunity for our fans to show up and make our atmosphere really special, and celebrate these seniors as we get an opportunity to compete." Maintaining Focus Question: You always talk about trying to not make the moment bigger than it is, but senior day, huge rivalry, the postseason implications; how do you reiterate to your team to take this one day at a time and not focus on making it too big? DL: "Yeah, just remind them of reality. It wasn't that long ago that we were kind of thrown to the curb, and that's all changed because they were able to focus on what's right in front of them. I think that the secret here is to continue to do what you've done the last few weeks and focus on what you control and what you're in charge of, and do a good job in those moments." Free Saturday Q: Curious what the Saturday was like. Different case where you play on Friday, and then the reaction to the fallout and how that changed things. What was Saturday like? item.title: ManningCast has perfect reaction to Bengals-Commanders power outage
item.description: There have been plenty of issues with various systems across the country in recent weeks, and now it’s made its way to Monday Night Football . During the NFL Week 11 finale between the Cincinnati Bengals and Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium, there was a temporary blackout. The power in the stadium went out at exactly 10:00 p.m. ET, as Jayden Daniels was set to take a snap on third down. MORE: Stefon Diggs sideline meltdown wakes up Commanders offense on ‘MNF’ Suddenly, it was pitch black, and no one knew how long the delay would last. The Lights Go Out In Bengals Vs. Commanders. Literally Right As Jayden Daniels Was About To Snap It. On 3rd And 14. Sometimes When This Happens, It Just Can’t Be A Coincidence. Somebody’s Gotta Be Doing This On Purpose. And Damn, It’s Dark In There. Somebody Check The Breaker Box. 👀 — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) November 24, 2026 Luckily, it was only a matter of minutes until the lights were back on, and we now know the reason. As it turns out, the lighting vendor forgot today’s game was on a weekday, so scheduled maintenance ran its course. “The lighting vendor never disabled the regularly scheduled maintenance for 10 PM. It’s a weekday thing, and they forgot it was a Monday night game ,” Joe Buck said on the broadcast. Luckily, we had the ManningCast to get us through the moment, and when the lights came back on, we got the perfect response. MORE: Laura Rutledge rocks jaw-dropping gown for special CMA red carpet gig Peyton & Eli Manning Deliver Perfect Reaction To Power Outage "It’s like Clark Griswold in Christmas Vacation!" Peyton and Eli Manning react to the power being restored during Bengals-Commanders 😭🎄 https://t.co/RBlGOXsKCW — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) November 24, 2026 “Video of the lights turning on. No, look at that. Just popped right on. Just like a switch,” Eli said. Peyton responded, “You think there’s like a switch in there and someone just hits it? It’s like Clark Griswold in Christmas Vacation .” Well played, fellas. Ratings for the ManningCast may be down this season, but it’s moments like this that remind us why we have come to love it. item.title: Lakers forward turned to Flavor Flav to fix his jump shot
item.description: A week ago, Lakers big man Sandro Mamukelashvili put together a 1-10 shooting performance against the Jazz and immediately went to address his struggles. Mamukelashvili said that he was working out in the Lakers practice facility to work on his shooting deficiencies, and was joined by his good friend, 67-year-old iconic rap artist Flavor Flav, who was in attendance watching his performance that night. Mamu’s friend, Flava Flav, came and rebounded for him in the middle of the night. He could tell Mamu was trying to work through his shot, so tried to be respectful of his mood. Mamu: “He’s always so loud, but he saw how intense I was … So he was like **whispers** “yeahh boyy” https://t.co/sjUWdCM4lP pic.twitter.com/bBgcykrzjY — Dave McMenamin (@mcten) November 23, 2026 “It was so funny because Flav was with me, so, he is always so loud. But he saw how intense I was when I came here and so he was like (softly) ‘Yeah, boy,” Mamukelashvili said. “It was cool actually, he was out there trying to rebound. So, shoutout to him for coming to the gym. It was cool.” The practice with Flavor Flav must’ve paid off for Mamukelashvili. Sandro Mamukelashvili lining up for a free throw against the Jazz. NBAE via Getty Images During Friday’s 106-104 victory against the Kings, he was 4-8 from the field and scored nine shots, while picking up nine rebounds. The relationship between Mamukelashvili and Flavor Flav dates all the way back to 2021 when he was selected by the Milwaukee Bucks in the second round of the 2021 NBA Draft. Flavor Flav and Sandro Mamukelashvili greeting one another before the Lakers play in an NBA game against the Hornets. NBAE via Getty Images The two met through Mamukelashvili’s financial adviser during the NBA’s summer league games. According to Khobi Price of the California Post , the two’s friendship developed, and the two New York natives have gone to Yankees games together and have dinner with each other. US rapper Flavor Flav arrives for the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony in Los Angeles on Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026. CONNOR TERRY/EPA/Shutterstock Mamukelashvili told Price that Flavor Flav has always “[had] this positive impact” on him and is always “hyped.” While Mamukelashvili has been working on his shot with his longtime friend, he is looking for redemption on Monday night, as the Lakers and Jazz are currently playing against each other.

item.title: Islanders blow two-goal lead in embarassing loss that gave Maple Leafs first win this month
item.description: Toronto Maple Leafs center Dakota Joshua reacts after scoring a goal against the New York Islanders on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, at UBS Arena in Elmont, N.Y. There is only so bad a loss can be in the NHL before Thanksgiving, but the Islanders got pretty close to the limit Monday night. Not only did they blow a two-goal lead on home ice to woeful Maple Leafs side that took its first victory in the month of November, 4-2 after losing nine in a row, but the Islanders lost top-line winger Kyle Palmieri to injury as well. Just as the Islanders were getting healthy — and after the Maple Leafs looked utterly hapless through the first 20 minutes of this game — it was a brutal 1-2 punch. Toronto Maple Leafs center Dakota Joshua reacts after scoring a goal against the New York Islanders on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, at UBS Arena in Elmont, N.Y. Robert Sabo for NY Post Palmieri exited early in the second period when his right leg wrapped around the Leafs’ goal post while he was colliding with Easton Cowan. Having torn his left ACL last year, Palmieri didn’t put weight on his right skate while coming off the ice, and walked up the tunnel under his own power. The Islanders declared him out for the rest of the night with a lower-body injury. In the immediate aftermath, they didn’t look too deterred, with Mathew Barzal scoring a highlight-reel goal to open his account for the season. His curl up the wall and subsequent dance through William Nylander and Aatu Raty before scoring to put the Islanders up 2-0 6:55 into the second was vintage stuff — a burst of inspiration and individual creativity that few players around the league are capable of. It was also the last good moment the Islanders would have on a night that, to that point, had looked fairly straightforward. The two teams seemed to do a body swap. The Islanders were suddenly losing battles, managing the puck poorly and struggling to generate much of anything. Toronto’s Dakota Joshua deflected Jake McCabe’s shot past Ilya Sorokin to cut it to 2-1 at 10:14 of the second, and the Islanders couldn’t rid themselves of any passivity. By the time Chris Tanev ripped a shot to tie it at two at 3:52 of the third, it felt like the Maple Leafs had been knocking on the door for a while. New York Islanders goaltender Ilya Sorokin (30) deflects the puck against the Toronto Maple Leafs on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, at UBS Arena in Elmont, N.Y. item.title: 4 Reasons Why 76ers’ Winning Streak Ended In Blowout Loss To Trail Blazers
item.description: Nov 23, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) passes the ball against the Portland Trail Blazers during the second quarter at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images On the back of a 132-129 win over the Milwaukee Bucks , the Philadelphia 76ers had extended their winning streak to five games, boasting considerable momentum entering Monday night’s matchup. Unfortunately, things did not play out well for Philadelphia, as the Portland Trail Blazers snapped their winning streak in a blowout 128-111 victory. The 76ers simply looked outmatched on Monday night. Although the performances from the superstar trio of LeBron James (23 PTS, 6 REB, 3 AST), Tyrese Maxey (22 PTS, 5 AST), and Jaylen Brown (20 PTS, 4 AST, 2 STL) were noteworthy, they were not enough to contain the offensive barrage from Deni Avdija and Damian Lillard , who combined for 49 points. With this loss, Philadelphia finds itself falling to 14-4 on the season. While this sees them retain their place at the top of the Eastern Conference leaderboard, some points from Monday night’s performance may need addressing to prevent a potential losing slide. On that note, here are four reasons the 76ers failed to secure the win against the Trail Blazers. The Lack Of A True Big Man Was Evident One of the factors that stood out during Monday night’s game was the impact of the big man. With Joel Embiid sidelined , the Philadelphia 76ers opted to start Jabari Walker at center, allowing Dean Wade to come off the bench. In principle, this has proven to be a solid tactic because of Walker’s athleticism, versatility, and hustle. Unfortunately, against Blazers center Donovan Clingan , this wasn’t the case. Although Walker did a solid job, posting 10 points and five rebounds for the game, he was clearly outplayed by his positional matchup. To that end, when considering that Clingan notched 15 points and 18 rebounds for the game, the Blazers center single-handedly dominated on the glass, helping Portland win the rebounding battle 49-33. While the small-ball approach has merit, against a team with an established center like the Blazers, Philadelphia found itself struggling. Given that the repercussions were felt more tangibly in the second half, the 76ers’ need for a true center in the rotation in such situations is evident. Perimeter Shooting Defined The Game Although Clingan’s dominance on the rebounding and defensive front swayed the result in Portland’s favor, it was the perimeter shooting from both teams that ultimately defined the game. Even though the Philadelphia 76ers aren’t known as a phenomenal three-point shooting team, their average of 34.9% shooting from beyond the arc is respectable enough to position them as a threat. In this regard, the early segments of the game even saw some promising production. Unfortunately, this did not last long. After a solid start, the 76ers’ efficiency from three-point range disappeared. Regardle

item.title: SEC to hold vote on terminating LSU from conference
item.description: BATON ROUGE, LA - NOVEMBER 7: A detail of a yard marker with the South Eastern Conference logo used during a game between the LSU Tigers and the Alabama Crimson Tide at Tiger Stadium on November 7, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The talk over the last five months has centered on the eligibility of players heading into a fifth season. The NCAA has allowed players from all classes moving forward to play for five seasons in collegiate athletics, but that is not the case for seniors who graduated this past May. Fast forward, and after numerous injunctions and back-and-forths in the courtroom, we are seeing players take the court in college basketball. One of the most prominent examples of this has been RJ Luis at LSU. After playing one game for Will Wade, the LSU President recently shut him down. Now, it appears the SEC is looking to hold up its end of the bargain, as it said it would if LSU played him. According to a statement put out by the SEC, they intend to hold a vote of league presidents to consider terminating LSU from the SEC. That will happen on December 3rd. If we are being honest, it would be a total shell shock if the SEC voted out LSU, so it is more than likely not going to happen. But the fact that Greg Sankey is standing his ground on this makes it even clearer that it would have been a fight to get Mark Mitchell eligible for the Cats this season. NEW: The SEC intends to hold a vote of league presidents to consider terminating LSU's membership, the conference announced. https://t.co/xznS7i3Djl pic.twitter.com/TgjXagtduf — On3 (@On3) November 23, 2026

item.title: Peter Obi lacks capacity to manage people properly — Abure
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Factional National Chairman of the Labour Party (LP), Julius Abure has accused Peter Obi of lacking the capacity to unite and manage people, citing the departure of several figures who worked with the party’s 2023 presidential candidate. Abure made the allegation on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, while explaining his fallout with Obi and his decision to support President Bola Tinubu. “Peter Obi doesn’t have capacity to manage people properly. I ask you, the structure we built around him in the 2023 general election. Where are the people? Where is Yunusa Tanko? He is in another party. You are looking at me because I’m saying I’m supporting Bola Tinubu. Yunusa Tanko is no longer with Peter,” Abure said. “Ask yourself what happened to Yunusa Tanko. Ask yourself where is Sarah Ibrahim? Where is his vice-presidential candidate in the 2023 general election? Where are a lot of others? Where is people like Valentine Ozigbo? There are many others. The man simply does not have the capacity, the character, and competence to put people together and galvanise them towards achieving a set goal.” Abure denied ever frustrating Obi out of the Labour party, saying the party had given him substantial control after the 2023 election. He argued that Obi’s experience with political parties and the Obidient movement showed, in his view, that he had struggled to keep people together. “There was no frustration, we gave him everything. We practically handed over the leadership of the party to him, and that was the truth of the matter. If you go and find out, you are journalists. I’m sure a lot of your people were with us during the campaign. “After the campaign, I practically almost handed over the party for him to run, and the result is what you have seen,” he said. “Peter Obi himself will tell you: Look at people’s past. Look at Obi’s past. Look at APGA, look at PDP, look at Labour now, and look at the people that are with him, even in the Obidient movement, how they have all abandoned him and left him because he doesn’t have that capacity to put people together and manage them for effective performance.” Abure also said his experience working with Obi, who is now contesting the 2027 election under the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), had convinced him that the former Anambra governor was “unstable” and “unreliable.” He said he chose to support Tinubu ahead of the 2027 elections because he believed the president was better suited to lead. “You see, experience they say is the best teacher. Now I have experience working with Peter Obi, and I have seen him in and out that he is unstable, unreliable, a pretender cannot be trusted because of the way he treated the leadership of the party,” Abure added. “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is 100% better. And I give you the analysis today. Today, we gave a comparative analysis of the personality of Peter Obi and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, giving our experiences now, and all the party members

item.title: 970m Africans lack access to clean cooking — Energy expert
item.description: By Ediri Ejoh & Henry Obetta About 970 million Africans lack access to clean cooking, while over 560 million people in sub-Saharan Africa are without electricity, energy experts have said, calling for greater continental collaboration to tackle the crisis. Regional Chair for Africa of the World Energy Council, Mr Omar Farouk, disclosed this at the 14th anniversary lecture and investiture into the Realnews Hall of Fame, organised by Realnews Magazine, with the theme: “Geopolitical Turbulence and Energy Security: Forging Strategic Opportunities for Africa.” Citing the 2026 Tracking SDG 7 Report, based on 2024 data, Farouk lamented Africa’s energy poverty despite its abundant oil, gas and renewable resources. “How can a continent so richly endowed with energy resources remain so energy poor? Why do petroleum-producing countries sometimes struggle to supply affordable fuels to their own citizens? Why do countries with natural gas resources suffer from electricity shortages?” he asked. He attributed the crisis largely to inadequate finance, technology and infrastructure, rather than resource scarcity. “We cannot, as a continent, be able to get out of where we have found ourselves today if we continue to operate in silos. Our solution lies in cooperation and collaboration,” he said. Farouk stressed that finance, technology and infrastructure must work together to drive energy development, adding: “You can have a lot of money without the technology, you can’t make any progress. You can bring scientists, technologists, without the money, they can’t make progress. And you can have both of these without the energy infrastructure, you can’t move energy from one point to the other.” He said Africa was projected to attract only $110 billion, or 3.3 per cent of the estimated $3.4 trillion global energy investment in 2026, while universal clean cooking access would require about $4 billion annually. Managing Director of Frazimex Engineering Limited, a subsidiary of Oilserv Group, Engr. Chuka Eze, urged African countries to leverage global geopolitical disruptions to strengthen energy sovereignty and industrial capacity. He said Africa captures less than one per cent of the value generated from clean-energy technology manufacturing, despite its rich mineral resources. “Africa’s opportunity is to move from being a supplier of strategic resources to becoming a shaper of the global energy system,” Eze said. He called for stronger local-content policies, technology transfer, skills development and regional cooperation to promote domestic processing, manufacturing and industrial growth. The post 970m Africans lack access to clean cooking — Energy expert appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: St. Louis CITY SC hold off LAFC to earn historic playoff win
item.description: By Ari Liljenwall St. Louis CITY SC opened their Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs campaign with a 3-2 victory over LAFC in Game 1 of their Western Conference Round One Best-of-3 Series on Monday night at Energizer Park, twice fending off comeback bids from the visitors. Daniel Edelman , Sang Bin Jeong and Simon Becher scored for St. Louis, while Sergi Palencia and Denis Bouanga tallied for Black & Gold. The result gives CITY SC a 1-0 series lead heading into Game 2 at BMO Stadium, where they'll have a chance to book a Western Conference Semifinal matchup against either FC Dallas or the Portland Timbers . St. Louis CITY SC hold off LAFC to earn historic playoff win St. Louis opened the scoring in the 35th minute, as Edelman rifled home a first-time finish off a cutback from Rafael Navarro , who had sent a golden opportunity wide earlier in the first half. The hosts doubled their advantage in the 51st minute through Jeong, who fired a shot from the top of the penalty area that went in off the post. Becher netted the eventual match-winner in the 78th minute, punishing an LAFC giveaway with a first-time strike from outside the box. LAFC twice cut the deficit to one, first through Sergi Palencia 's glancing header in the 62nd minute and again through Denis Bouanga 's 85th-minute penalty kick, but St. Louis held on for the victory. Goals 35' - STL - Daniel Edelman | WATCH 51' - STL - Jeong Sang-bin | WATCH 62' - LAFC - Sergi Palencia | WATCH 78' - STL - Simon Becher | WATCH 85' - LAFC - Denis Bouanga (PK) | WATCH Lineups Three Things THE BIG PICTURE: St. Louis made club history with their first-ever playoff victory, continuing a remarkable turnaround under first-year head coach Yoann Damet. Despite twice seeing their two-goal advantage cut in half, CITY SC held firm to move within one win of reaching their first Western Conference Semifinal MOMENT OF THE MATCH: What initially looked like an insurance tally from Becher in the 78th minute proved to be the difference. MAN OF THE MATCH: Jeong provided a moment of individual brilliance with his 51st-minute strike, giving CITY SC a two-goal advantage and setting the tone for their historic postseason victory. Next Up STL: Saturday, Nov. 28 at LAFC | 8:30 pm ET (Apple TV) | Round One Best-of-3 Series, Game 2 LAFC: Saturday, Nov. 28 vs. St. Louis CITY SC | 8:30 pm ET (Apple TV) | Round One Best-of-3 Series, Game 2

item.title: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels injures hand vs Bengals Monday night
item.description: Washington Commanders starting quarterback Jayden Daniels suffered an apparent hand injury during the third quarter of the team's NFL Week 11 game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Northwest Stadium on ESPN's Monday Night Football. Daniels injured his non-throwing hand and was seen icing it on the sideline during the game. ESPN sideline reporter Laura Rutledge said Daniels also had the hand wrapped briefly. Daniels returned to the game after trainers treated the injury. Daniels entered the game as the Commanders' leading rusher this season with 280 yards on 42 carries through seven games. During the Bengals-Commanders preseason game in 2025, MNF analyst Troy Aikman criticized Bengals defensive back Jordan Battle for not hitting Daniels on the QB's first-quarter touchdown run. In a 2024 battle between former LSU quarterbacks who won Heisman Trophies, Daniels outdueled the Bengals' Joe Burrow. Burrow finished with more passing yards, but Daniels completed 21 of his 23 attempts and added 39 rushing yards and a touchdown on the ground. It was the first NFL game since 1940 with no turnovers and no punts. This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels injures hand vs Bengals Monday night

item.title: CJ Rosser signs with North Carolina
item.description: Last Thursday, it was reported that Kentucky Basketball had removed itself from the race for the No. 2 overall player in the 2027 recruiting class, CJ Rosser, because the price was getting too high. Now, on Monday night, it was reported that Rosser, a 6-foot-10, 200-pound 5-star forward, signed with North Carolina during last week’s early signing period, according to Joe Tipton of Rivals. While it is disappointing that Kentucky was unable to land a commitment from Rosser, the Wildcats have still made progress in the 2027 recruiting class, securing commitments from two 4-star prospects in small forward Ryan Hampton and center Cherif Millogo. That is a much better position than Kentucky was in at this point last year. The Wildcats did not receive their first commitment in the 2026 class until April, when 4-star point guard Mason Williams pledged to Mark Pope and his staff. With the 2027 recruiting class potentially nearing its conclusion for Kentucky, the Wildcats could turn their attention toward a potential reclassification candidate from the 2028 class, which would be an interesting development to monitor.

item.title: Player Grades: Cavs at Bulls – Poor effort results in a rough loss
item.description: CHICAGO, IL - NOVEMBER 23: Donovan Mitchell of the Cleveland Cavaliers #45 reacts after making a basket during an NBA game against the Chicago Bulls on November 23, 2026 at the United Center in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Melissa Tamez/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cleveland Cavaliers fell behind by 22 points in the first half of this game as they blew an easy one against the Chicago Bulls. Grades are based on our usual expectations for each player. Player of the game Donovan Mitchell 28 points, 3 rebounds, 5 assists, 2 blocks, 1 steal Mitchell was largely absent for most of this game. His impact wasn’t felt until the third and fourth quarters, when he grew more aggressive in trying to will his team back into the game. His scoring was too little, too late, as the Cavs lost this game when Chicago outscored them 45-20 in the second quarter. Still, he takes our player of the game for getting to the line 12 times and converting all but one of those free throw attempts. Grade: C- Grades James Harden 21 points, 6 rebounds, 5 assists, 7 turnovers Harden got the Cavs back into this game through his downhill drives in the third quarter. He was as important as anyone in turning the tide after that ugly second quarter. With that said, Harden shares just as much blame for their collapse in the first half. Turnovers and missed shots led to easy transition buckets for Chicago. And his half-court defense wasn’t making up for anything. Grade: D+ Jarrett Allen 16 points, 4 rebounds, 1 block Cleveland could have done a better job of finding Allen. He shot 6-for-7 from the floor but wasn’t fed the ball enough for my liking. We know that Allen can quickly build momentum when he’s being featured in the offense, and the Cavs never really tapped into that tonight. Still, Allen failed to seize the one aspect of this that is within his control — offensive rebounding. Allen could have had more touches tonight if he had cleaned the offensive glass. Instead, he finishes with only 4 rebounds (1 offensive). Grade: D+ Peyton Watson 8 points, 10 rebounds, 3 assists, 6 blocks The Cavs have something real in Watson’s ability to block shots as a weakside defender. He’s been a genuinely impactful defender in these scenarios. But there are more holes in the ship than just that, and so far, Watson hasn’t been enough to stop the sinking. Cleveland will need to get better support at the point-of-attack and in transition before getting the most out of Watson’s defense. Grade: B – Tyrese Proctor 4 points, 2 rebounds, 2 assists Proctor is readjusting to his role now that Harden and Mitchell have taken back full control of the offense. He hasn’t been as prominently featured as a creator, and that’s led to quieter performances as of late. He’s done well in this smaller role, but the Cavs should look for more ways to enable Proctor as this feels like they are currently selling him short. item.title: Five athlete-team disputes in Bay Area that predate Brandon Aiyuk's stare-down with 49ers
item.description: Chris Webber #4 goes up to a make a basket during the Golden State Warriors vs. Portland Trail Blazers game on Sunday at the Oracle Arena in Oakland, Calif., on March 2, 2008. Photo by Lea Suzuki / San Francisco Chronicle (Lea Suzuki/S.F. Chronicle) The San Francisco 49ers ' long, tumultuous contract dispute with Brandon Aiyuk came to an end on Monday when the team waived the wide receiver. It already rates as one of the most contentious confrontations between player and team in Bay Area sports history. This all started in 2024 with Aiyuk requesting a trade amid contract extension talks. Then ACL and MCL tears in his right knee during Week 7 of the 2024 NFL season - seven games into his freshly-signed $120 million extension - further complicated the relationship. Aiyuk failed to fulfill his rehabilitation and team participation responsibilities, prompting the 49ers to void nearly $27 million of guaranteed money. That led to a series of public outbursts from Aiyuk; he posted on social media pictures of himself in Washington Commanders gear asking for a trade, posted video of himself appearing to speed down the street near Levi's Stadium in his car, and disparaged team leadership. Aiyuk stopped reporting to the 49ers entirely and the team made it clear the 28-year-old would not be invited back. Contract terms are still in flux after the divorce with the 49ers seeking $13 million of his bonus money reimbursed. It has been an odd saga, but it's also not the first time a disgruntled athlete made a stink about his relationship with a Bay Area team and the money he's owed. Here are five other times something similar happened. Wide receiver Terrell Owens played his first eight NFL seasons with the 49ers, but left for Philadelphia after a dispute with the team. (Lance Iversen/S.F. Chronicle) Terrell Owens versus 49ers, 2004: Tension had been growing between star wide receiver Terrell Owens and the 49ers. Owens, openly ready to part ways with his longtime team after years of blow ups and acrimony, planned to void the final three years of his contract and become a free agent by the March deadline in 2004. His agent, however, didn't realize the deadline to void had moved from March to Feb. 21 and reportedly missed the deadline, which meant the 49ers maintained they technically still had the rights to Owens. And they planned on taking advantage. The 49ers pulled together a trade that would send Owens to the Baltimore Ravens for a second-round pick in the 2004 draft. Owens, believing he was a free agent, had negotiated terms to join the Philadelphia Eagles. The NFL Players Association intervened, and the dispute went to arbitration. The Ravens got out of the entire transaction. Owens wound up in Philadelphia, but before the Eagles sent a fifth-round pick to Baltimore and defensive end Brandon Whiting to the 49ers as compensation. Owens signed a seven-year, $49 million deal with the Eagles. The 49ers got something out of the debacle, and Owens got out of San Fr

item.title: Ajaokuta: NES blames collapse of long-term planning for 40-year stalemate
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The President, Nigerian Economic Society (NES), Dr. Baba Musa, has blamed the collapse of long-term economic planning for the failure of the Ajaokuta Steel Company to become operational more than four decades after its establishment. Musa, who spoke at the National Growth & Development Forum (NGDF) 2026 in Abuja, said Nigeria lost the link between economic planning and execution, resulting in the abandonment or underperformance of strategic national projects. “History demands candour. Somewhere along the way, we lost vital links between plan and performance. We built, but did not always maintain,” he said. According to him, the oil windfall of the 1970s diverted the country from agriculture and non-oil exports which had previously sustained the economy. “The oil windfall of the 1970s drew us away from the agriculture and non-oil exports that had sustained us. Strategic projects such as the Ajaokuta Steel Complex, begun with great promise, have yet to fulfil it four decades on. “And when formal planning gave way in the mid-1980s, long-term strategy too often yielded to visions that changed with administrations,” Musa said. He said Nigeria must learn from its past policy failures to avoid repeating mistakes that have undermined economic development. “The Nigeria we want must be built upon the Nigeria we have, and the Nigeria we have,” he added. The NES president also expressed concern that economic reforms had yet to translate into shared prosperity, noting that about 63 per cent of Nigerians, estimated at 140 million people, lived below the poverty line in 2025, according to the World Bank. “Macroeconomic stability is necessary, but it is not yet shared prosperity. A stable exchange rate is not yet a full dinner table. Stability is the foundation; it is not the building,” he said. Musa called for an economy that generates jobs, supports the poor, boosts domestic production, invests in human capital and promotes disciplined public finance and credible institutions. Similarly, President, Capital Market Academics of Nigeria, Prof. Uche Uwaleke, said economic reforms must be measured by their impact on citizens’ welfare, job creation, purchasing power and poverty reduction. The post Ajaokuta: NES blames collapse of long-term planning for 40-year stalemate appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: Rick Scuteri-Imagn Images How Brandon Williams’ expected return can energize Stephen Curry-less Warriors offense appeared first on ClutchPoints . Though Williams was initially viewed as a solid add to the Dubs’ point guard depth, signing a one-year, $2.62-million veteran minimum deal this past offseason, his change-of-pace, lightning-quick on-ball skills had become an important part of how Golden State’s offense functioned in the non-Curry minutes, minutes that typically dictate whether the Warriors can be serious contenders in the Western Conference arms race. In the somewhat limited 158 minutes Williams has been on the floor, Golden State has scored an additional +12.1 points per 100 possessions , which ranks in the 94th percentile among all players in the league and ties Curry for most on the team, according to Cleaning the Glass. Additionally, there’s been very little drop-off from Curry to Williams. With Kerr staggering Curry and Williams to ensure at least one of them is on the floor at all times, the Warriors only suffer a 3.5 point/100 poss. drop-off , as Curry’s +13.9 net rating to Williams’ +10.4 net rating remains well into the positives according to Databallr. And perhaps the most eye-opening advanced metric is how the Warriors are a -29.1 net rating when neither Curry or Williams are on the floor. item.title: Steve Kerr’s Rant Against Flopping Takes Ironic Turn as Warriors Star Gets Fined By NBA
item.description: IMAGO / Marty Jean Louis ©Credit - Imago The drama surrounding the Sunday night match-up between Warriors and Celtics doesn’t seem to end. Even after a day, the refs came back with a jab aimed at the Dubs. Today, Steve Kerr has made his frustration with NBA flopping increasingly clear this season, even suggesting that the Warriors may have to adopt the same tactics to keep up with their opponents. But the comments took an ironic turn. Just hours after the Warriors coach joked about teaching defenders to exaggerate contact, the NBA announced a fine for one of his own players. The league fined backup guard Will Richard $2,000 for flopping during Sunday’s 88–87 victory over the Boston Celtics. The violation occurred with 8:47 remaining in the second quarter, when Richard was defending Payton Pritchard, coming off a screen set by Neemias Quetta. No one noticed it then. Kerr's anti flopping crusade just backfired spectacularly. Subscribe for the NBA drama and coaching contradictions you won't see coming. However, the NBA announced the penalty roughly two hours after Kerr addressed reporters following practice. It created an awkward coincidence for a coach who had just spoken out against the very behavior that got his player fined. “I think we probably have to start teaching our defensive players to flop on screens because everybody around the league is doing it,” Kerr said. “You know, you set a screen and guys chase around the screen and act like they’ve been hit by a car, and the whole bench jumps up. And those are automatic fouls. So we’ve got to start teaching that.” Kerr also argued that the league could eliminate the problem by enforcing its rules more consistently. “I’ve said this many times. Just eliminate the (expletive), and the players will stop doing it. But they don’t eliminate it, and so players keep doing it.” Warriors’ guard Richard’s fine came after the league reviewed his defensive sequence against Pritchard. The Celtics guard drove toward the paint and attempted a shot off the glass, while Richard appeared to exaggerate the contact and go to the floor. Pritchard missed, and Georges Niang collected the rebound. The officials did not penalize Richard during the game, leaving the league office to assess the play afterward. This is part of the NBA’s 2026–27 emphasis on curbing flopping. When officials identify a violation during a game, they can assess a technical foul for theatrics and award the opposing team a free throw. If the league identifies an uncalled violation through its postgame review, it can issue a fine instead. Richard was not the only Warrior involved in a controversial attempt to draw a call against Boston. With 1:07 remaining in the fourth quarter, Brandin Podziemski made a clutch 4-point play; it initially appeared to be a crucial three-pointer while drawing a foul from Baylor Scheierman. I’m super grateful to just be a part of this group of girls and staff. It just felt like such a family. item.title: Bengals-Commanders officials miss Treylon Burks' facemask Monday night
item.description: Commanders receiver Treylon Burks got away with grabbing Bengals defensive back Dax Hill's facemask as Hill defended Burks on a pass during the third quarter of their NFL Week 11 game at Northwest Stadium on ESPN's Monday Night Football. "Looked like Burks had a hold of (Dax Hill)," MNF analyst Troy Aikman said during the broadcast. Earlier in the game, Aikman said rainy conditions during the first half were benefitting the Commanders by keeping Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow from trying to throw downfield. During the Bengals-Commanders preseason game in 2025, MNF analyst Troy Aikman criticized Bengals defensive back Jordan Battle for not hitting Daniels on the QB's first-quarter touchdown run. Weeks later, Aikman disagreed when Bengals center Ted Karras was called for a crucial false-start penalty during the first quarter of the team's NFL Week 4 loss to Denver at Empower Field at Mile High. Aikman also called the Bengals' offense a mess during the Denver game. In December 2024, Aikman said his NFL MVP vote would go to Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow. And Buck and Aikman agreed that officials missed an obvious penalty when the Dallas Cowboys ' Marist Liufau grabbed Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow's facemask during the fourth quarter of Cincinnati's NFL Week 14 win at AT&T Stadium on Monday Night Football. The Bengals and Commanders met on Monday night during the 2024 regular season. Buck said it was a must-win game for Cincinnati after an 0-2 start. Washington won 38-33 . During the Saints-Chiefs Monday Night Football game in 2024, Buck trolled the Bengals and punter Ryan Rehkow's errant hold in a loss against Baltimore. Buck and Aikman also called the Bengals' overtime win against the Jacksonville Jaguars in December 2023. item.title: Cisco and OpenAI pitch eBPF kernel plugins as the way to tame the patchpocalypse
item.description: Cisco and OpenAI have released an open-source tool called Shirudo to implement compensating controls in Linux, potentially improving security for users who can’t quickly patch newly discovered software flaws. Shirudo relies on eBPF, the technology that makes it possible to run sandboxed programs in the Linux kernel. eBPF programs are effectively kernel plug-ins but don’t get unrestricted access to system resources. Developers have mostly used eBPF to create network functions that enable things like the open source Kubernetes observability and security tool Cilium , a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project. Cisco and OpenAI think eBPF can help organizations cope with the flood of 100,000-plus software flaws reported this year, many after the debut of AI-powered bug finders. The increased volume of flaws, and patches to fix them, is a problem for many organizations which already struggle to test fixes or find change windows in which to implement them. That problem has seen greater interest in “compensating controls” – changes to applications or infrastructure that harden them against flaws or malware, without requiring a patch. With Shirudo, Cisco and OpenAI are suggesting two things: The privileges eBPF programs enjoy make them a fine way to implement compensating controls for Linux; Agents should scan your infrastructure for vulnerabilities, then use tools like OpenAI’s Codex to write compensating controls as eBPF programs at machine speed. “Shirudo” is apparently the Japanese word for “shield,” so Cisco and OpenAI have called the eBPF programs the tool creates “shields.” The two companies envision humans checking every shield Shirudo creates before putting it into production. Shirudo is open source and available here . The two companies say they’ve already demonstrated it could mitigate the recently discovered flaws in Java without requiring downtime for an Elasticsearch implementation. Cisco and OpenAI are not alone in advocating for compensating controls. Third-party software maintenance outfits like Rimini Street have used them for years to protect software when their clients no longer have the right to access patches. VMware has introduced “virtual patching.” Palo Alto Networks and Rapid 7 also like this approach, and offer automation to develop controls. Where Cisco and OpenAI differ is their decision to make Shirudo open source , and their ambition that other players adapt and advance it. That offer is not entirely altruistic, as if Shirudo takes off it could create more demand for Codex. Cisco’s angle comes from the fact it owns Isovalent, an early champion of eBPF and the creator of both Cilium and the Tetragon sub-project on which Shirudo is based. Switchzilla is using eBPF in other products, so normalizing its use through an open source project can’t hurt. ®

item.title: Anthropic says Claude solved an age-old math problem, but the written proof is 250,000 pages of slop
item.description: The leaders of the great model houses, Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman, desperately want the world to believe AI is the skeleton key which will unlock the secrets of the universe. But if the AI can’t explain what it’s “proven,” are we actually any closer to understanding anything, or have we simply built another black box? That question is top of mind among mathematicians and computer scientists this week after Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge claimed to have solved a mathematical conjecture so elusive it's gone unproven for more than 150 years. The fact that this note came out one day after Anthropic's record-setting IPO is a coincidence, we're sure. In a four-page post to his website, the researcher described how with the help of Claude, he believes he has proven the Riemann Hypothesis, one of seven Millennium problems so complex and so important that the Clay Mathematics Institute has offered a $1 million prize to anyone who is successful in solving them. The Riemann Hypothesis, conjectured by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, contends that all nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function – those with a real part between zero and one – have a real part equal to 1/2. Confused? Don’t worry. We’ve linked to an explainer that goes into more detail here . What's important is that, if the Riemann Hypothesis is right, mathematicians can place tighter bounds on the difference between the actual distribution of prime numbers and mathematical estimates of that distribution. Researchers have previously attempted to disprove the conjecture through computational brute force, and therein have shown the hypothesis holds to at least 10 trillion zeros . There’s reason to believe that the Riemann Hypothesis is accurate, but the possibility remains that over a sufficiently long series the pattern might diverge. And so, more than 150 years after Riemann published his hypothesis, it has remained just that. Alpöge’s proof, if it can even be called that, is now the subject of great debate. The four pages in which Alpöge remarks on the discoveries he and Claude made aren’t exactly a proof, but rather 14 tarballs worth of Lean code totaling roughly 240 MB. Lean is an open source programming language commonly used to help validate mathematical proofs. The Clay Mathematics Institute, which oversees the seven Millennium Problems, has promoted the Riemann Hypothesis from “unsolved” to “active” status, but it is not yet considered solved. For Clay to consider the problem solved and award the prize, the proposed solution must be published in a qualifying outlet, remain available for scrutiny for at least two years, and receive broad acceptance from the mathematics community. As it stands, Alpöge describes the 250,000 pages of text generated by the model for its written proof as a “massive unreadable travesty of ‘slop.’” Not long after Alpöge's remarks and Lean code were published, Stanford mathematician Ravi Vakil released a nearly 1,000-pag

item.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Federal Government has called for stronger implementation of healthy food policies to address malnutrition, micronutrient deficiencies and the rising burden of diet-related non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in the country. The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr. Iziaq Adekunle Salako, made the call on Monday while delivering the keynote address at the maiden National Healthy Food Week and Learning Conference 2026 in Abuja. The conference, themed, “Our Food, Our Health, Our Future,” was organised to promote healthier food systems and strengthen efforts to address nutrition-related health challenges. Represented by the ministry’s Permanent Secretary, Ms. Daju Kachollom, Salako said tackling the country’s nutrition and health challenges required stronger collaboration among government institutions, regulatory agencies, food manufacturers, health professionals, researchers, development partners, the media and consumers. He noted that food choices and the quality of food available in markets, schools, hospitals, workplaces and homes had significant implications for public health, workforce productivity, child development and national prosperity. The minister said the Federal Government had introduced several policies and regulatory measures to improve food safety and nutritional standards, including the Revised National Policy on Food Safety and Quality and its Implementation Plan (2023). He said the policy framework promoted food safety, food fortification, sodium reduction, elimination of industrially produced trans fats and healthier food procurement practices in public institutions. Salako also highlighted the National Guidelines for Sodium Reduction, the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control’s (NAFDAC) Read the Label Campaign and the development of front-of-pack nutrition labelling as measures to help consumers make informed food choices and encourage manufacturers to improve the nutritional quality of their products. On public food procurement, he said government institutions provided millions of meals annually through schools, hospitals, correctional centres, emergency shelters and National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) camps, making public procurement an important instrument for improving the country’s food environment. He urged relevant authorities to ensure effective implementation of the Bureau of Public Procurement’s National Guidelines for Public Procurement of Food and Related Services through adequate monitoring, accountability and capacity building. The minister also identified fiscal measures, including the sugar-sweetened beverage tax, as important tools for discouraging excessive consumption of sugary drinks and generating revenue for public health interventions. He advocated transparent allocation of part of the revenue to nutrition education, healthier food environments and the prevention of diet-related diseases. item.title: Will astronauts farm on the moon? Scientists successfully grow potatoes in simulated lunar dust
item.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

It's no secret that NASA is working towards a permanent presence on the moon. The space agency even plans to build a moon base for its astronauts to call home. But humans living inside lunar habitats around the clock will need three square meals a day, so researchers have been working on how to grow food on the moon. To that end, a team from the College of Agricultural Sciences at Oregon State University have been raising potatoes in simulated moon dust with promising results. The researchers published their findings Nov. 20 in the Microgravity science journal. "We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter," Aymeric Goyer, associate professor at OSU's Department of Botany and Plant Pathology, said in a statement . "That's an important step toward developing reliable food production systems that could support long-term human exploration of the moon." To grow the spuds, the scientists used five different materials that are similar to regolith , the dust and rocks that cover the moon's surface. The moon contains various regions with unique surface makeups, so the materials they used simulated regolith from both lunar mare and lunar highland regions. The secret ingredient was vermicompost, a soil that's rich in nutrients. The team added different levels of vermicompost to the simulated regolith to grow the potatoes. They figured out that fake regolith mixed with 30 percent vermicompost worked about as well as growing potatoes with regular soil. Oregon State University researchers David Handy and Aymeric Goyer studying potatoes grown in lunar regolith. (Image credit: Aymeric Goyer/David Handy/OSU) "We believe the compost helps balance some of the toxicity we see in lunar regolith by reducing plant exposure to harmful compounds," David Handy, a postdoctoral researcher in Goyer's lab, said in the same statement. The idea is that astronauts in the future could bring a little nutrient-rich soil with them and mix it with regolith to grow potatoes. After all, it'd cost a ton to ship all that food from Earth. NASA funding supported this research.

item.title: Inception - possibly a ShinyHunters reboot - claims seven victims in a week
item.description: Don't mind the recent arrests. The ShinyHunters extortion gang may still be operating, just under the new name of Inception, according to Okta's threat intelligence group. ShinyHunters is the brash cybercriminal group that, most recently, breached rival gang Clop before hacking the FBI , resulting in at least three arrests of key suspects in September and October. The crims - and their old data leak site - have since gone dark. “While this threat cluster has changed their brand affiliation, the operators remain active in targeting organizations with voice phishing attacks and account takeovers resulting in data theft and extortion,” Okta threat hunters Moussa Diallo and Katie Nickels said on Monday. Okta tracks this threat cluster as O-UNC-053 - the “O-UNC” prefix stands for an Okta Uncategorized cluster, and it uses this label before formally attributing the activity to a named threat group. While Okta hasn't formally confirmed O-UNC-053 to be the same crime crew as ShinyHunters, the identity and access management provider’s researchers note that it does use nearly identical social engineering tactics: voice phishing , during which the scammers trick targets into entering credentials into phishing pages and approving multi-factor authentication (MFA). Plus, they note: O-UNC-053 operators change the themes of their phishing domains about every four to six weeks, and they also post claimed victims on ShinyHunters’ data leak site. In November, however, organizations targeted by O-UNC-053 began appearing on a new data leak site branded as Inception and not ShinyHunters. The first five - Advanced Micro Devices, Cigna Healthcare, Paychex, PepsiCo, and Henry Schein - appeared November 17 on the site, and all were marked “leaked.” Soon after, security maven Dominic Alvieri questioned if Inception was linked to ShinyHunters. “ShinyHunters are not all in jail,” he wrote on social media. On November 19, AutoZone appeared on the site, with Inception again claiming to have leaked the auto-parts retailer's files. On Saturday, EV technology firm Lucid Group joined the claimed victims. None of the seven companies have confirmed breaches, and none responded to The Register ’s inquiries. We will update this story when we receive more information. Okta Threat Intelligence “is unable to validate if published data is authentic,” the researchers said in response to our questions. In the Monday report, the Okta team does note that Inception’s new data leak site listings “included multiple targets for which Okta Threat Intelligence previously observed O-UNC-053 infrastructure registration.” The infrastructure was registered between six and 19 days before Inception listed the companies on its leak site, and this gap “is consistent with prior shifts from Com-affiliated actors,” Diallo and Nickels added. item.title: 2027: NUC proposes 4-week break for universities
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The National Universities Commission NUC has proposed that universities adopt a three-to-four-week break to accommodate the 2027 general election, saying the entire election cycle will last no more than four weeks. Executive Secretary of the NUC, Prof. Abdullahi Yusufu Ribadu, made the proposal on Monday in Abuja during a courtesy visit by the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN. According to a statement from INEC on Monday night, Amupitan was accompanied by National Commissioners and senior officials of the commission. The Presidential and National Assembly elections hold on Saturday, 16 January 2027. The Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections follow on Saturday, 6 February 2027. He noted that the academic community had for over a decade served as the backbone of collation and declaration of results, with Vice-Chancellors serving as Collation and Returning Officers across the Federation. The INEC Chairman said the commission had introduced operational, technological and security reforms to make the work of its university partners safer and less contentious. He said polling unit results on Form EC8A would undergo automated arithmetic consistency and over-voting checks before transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV). According to him, the commission has procured 57,000 new Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and lowered the voter-to-device ratio to 850 per machine. Amupitan added that INEC would conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Saturday, 28 November 2026. On security, he said the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) had been decentralised to every Local Government Area and Registration Area, with dedicated security cordons and escort protocols around collation centres. He drew attention to Sections 96 and 97 of the Electoral Act 2026, which criminalise violence, abusive rhetoric and threats against electoral personnel, and Section 148, which empowers the commission to prosecute offenders directly. “No Returning Officer or Collation Officer will be left to stand alone against lawlessness,” Amupitan said. He then asked the NUC for support in four areas: the timely nomination of academic staff of verified non-partisan standing, the alignment of academic calendars with the election dates, collaboration on voter education and counter-disinformation on campuses, and the welfare and recognition of academics deployed for election duty. Responding, Ribadu congratulated Amupitan on his appointment, describing him as a lawyer and academic of international repute and “a round peg in a round hole.” , The NUC Executive Secretary said the commission would engage Vice-Chancellors on the nomination of academic staff, including through an online meeting. item.title: The Apple Watch Series 12 is cheaper than ever ahead of Black Friday
item.description: The Apple Watch Series 12 is on sale in multiple configurations. | Photo: Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge If you’re still sporting an Apple Watch that launched five or so years ago, now is a good time to upgrade. Apple’s latest smartwatch, the 42mm Apple Watch Series 12 with Wi-Fi and GPS connectivity, has dropped to a new all-time low of $299 ($100 off) at Amazon and Walmart , beating its most sale price by $30. If you prefer a larger size, the 46mm model is on sale for $349 ($100 off) at Amazon and Walmart , beating its previous low by $30. Apple Watch Series 12 Where to Buy: $399 $299 at Amazon (GPS, 42mm) $399 $299 at Walmart (GPS, 42mm) $449 $349 at Amazon (GPS, 46mm) The Series 12 stands out compared to previous models with its new AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, which are made possible by Apple’s new S11 chip. For example, the watch can alert you when it detects sounds like a doorbell, alarm, or even a baby’s cry, while other upcoming features like Live Rewind and Siri Recap lets you look back at a transcript of the previous 15 seconds of conversation and get a high-level overview of the conversations you had that day. The new chip also makes Siri more responsive, so you can get answers to questions with less waiting around. It’s not all about AI, though. The Series 12 also features redesigned health sensors that can now track your heart rate every five seconds even when you’re not exercising, which is particularly help if you have a chronic condition and need to keep a closer eye on your heart rate. It also introduces a new readiness score to help you decide how prepared your body is for the day. Other highlights include easier navigation with simple pinch gestures, and faster charging, which helps to make up for the fact that battery life is rated at up to 24 hours on a single charge, just like the previous-generation model. In our testing, the watch went from 20 to 64 percent charge in just 20 minutes, making it relatively easy to top up while showering or getting ready for the day.
