item.title: States sue SpaceX to stop Grok from generating child sex images, revenge porn
item.description: On Monday, Virginia and Oregon became the first states to sue SpaceX, alleging that Grok continues to sexualize, unchecked, real photos of mostly women and children. SpaceX acquired xAI in February and now must handle the ongoing reckoning over the controversial rollout of Grok’s “spicy mode”—a model feature Musk hyped but was soon found to generate a flood of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) and child sex abuse images (CSAM). Initial safeguards were so lax that Grok sometimes generated nude images without being asked . Although X Safety and xAI (now known as SpaceXSI) were silent at first , Musk’s companies eventually apologized and claimed that additional safeguards were implemented and policies redesigned to block harmful outputs. However, state attorneys general alleged that those statements were “misleading” and that SpaceXSI instead quietly “embraced” sexualized content to seize more AI market share, as Grok continues to generate NCII and CSAM today. item.title: Amazon scoops up AI accelerator tech to keep chips busy at all times
item.description: Amazon has agreed to buy AI optimization technology from an Israeli startup in a bid to speed up its inference operations. The house of Bezos on Monday announced a deal to purchase proprietary AI acceleration tech from Decart AI, known as the Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), for an undisclosed amount. Amazon also plans to bring Decart’s three founders and their engineering team into the fold. Decart’s DOS is designed to push AI hardware closer to its maximum performance across different AI models and hardware platforms. The company claims that most AI chips live their lives without reaching their full potential – practically a sin in this age of increased hardware costs and limited availability – and DOS aims to fix that by operating between the model and the chip, optimizing kernels, compilers, and runtimes for the underlying hardware “so every core stays busy.” DOS is hardware-agnostic, with Decart saying it supports Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs, and, most critically for our purposes here, AWS Trainium chips. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost,” Peter DeSantis, Amazon SVP of foundational AI models, custom silicon, and quantum computing, said in the announcement. “That's the pillar Trainium and our AI efforts are built on, and from our earliest work with Decart, we knew they … would help us push it even further.” Decart doesn’t offer much in the way of details about its proprietary AI-maxxing tech, but claims it can reduce latency, improve throughput, and reduce the costs associated with training and inference runs. An Amazon spokesperson clarified to The Register that the deal is an asset purchase and not a full company acquisition, with Amazon only acquiring DOS and the tech behind it as well as personnel. As for what may become of Decart after the deal, that’s unclear. Amazon told us to reach out to Decart to learn what may happen to any remaining employees and the company’s other technology, but we didn’t hear back. Along with offering its optimization stack, Decart has a couple of different AI models: Lucy, a live video model marketed toward advertisers, live streamers, and the like; and Oasis, a world model AI marketed toward companies working on embodied AI applications. Decart’s non-DOS assets weren’t mentioned in the press release, and per the Amazon spokesperson we talked to, that means they weren’t part of the deal. We can’t imagine that the Decart team is too upset about the potential abandonment of those models, though: While neither company has disclosed a price, Bloomberg claims its sources value the deal at around $7.5 billion. If Bloomberg's figure is accurate, that would make this deal one of the most expensive in Amazon’s history, right between its $3.9 billion acquisition of One Medical and its $8.5 billion purchase of film studio MGM . ®

item.title: Trump backs Nvidia CEO’s return amid US lawmakers’ spy allegations, security concerns
item.description: US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia’s decision Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, as Democratic leaders vowed investigations and prominent Republicans questioned whether his return posed a national security risk. Trump also posted a doctored version of the famous photograph of him raising his fist after surviving a 2024 assassination attempt, replacing himself with Huang, who brandished a red bra beneath an Nvidia flag. The image appeared to allude to the scandal that forced Huang, co-founder of the AI chip giant, to resign less than two weeks earlier following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. “The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that the government had no reason to believe his return posed a national security risk. In a telephone interview with CNBC, Trump suggested the scandal could prove to be “a net positive” by highlighting Nvidia’s technological advances. “I don’t think he’s going to be diminished at all,” he said, predicting Huang would return at “an almost higher level.” He said the attorney general had confirmed that US authorities possessed no evidence Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct, but urged Nvidia to continue investigating its compliance with restrictions on advanced chip sales to China. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer and House speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries vowed sweeping investigations into Nvidia, Trump and his senior officials, with Jeffries singling out Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. “We will not allow America’s national security to be sold out by the Trump administration for personal financial gain,” Jeffries said. – ‘What changed?’ – Huang is already scheduled to face questioning behind closed doors by three House committees on December 1 over his relationship with the suspected Chinese intelligence operative and concerns about Nvidia’s chip exports. And the Republican-led Senate Banking Committee has announced that his appearance scheduled for December 3 will be livestreamed. “We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him,” said House Intelligence Committee Democrat Raja Krishnamoorthi, demanding a full public congressional hearing. Senator Elizabeth Warren called the decision “reckless” and demanded details of what input senior administration officials had provided in support of Huang’s return. Republican Senator John Curtis raised similar questions, noting that Nvidia’s board had reversed its opposition to reinstating Huang while an independent investigation remained unfinished. “Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board?” he wrote on X. “I’d like to know what changed.” Senator Pete Ricketts, also a Republican, said Huang’s behavior did not warrant reinstatement and insisted the move did not excuse him from testifying before Congress. item.title: Nigeria’s rice revolution collapses as 90 mills shutdown
item.description: *Paddy production volume crashes *From 75% self-sufficiency country goes into massive imports *Farmers abandon rice, move to other crops *Operators blame policy reversals, others *Why rice value chain now struggling —FG By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief, Jeff Agbodo (Abakiliki), Aliyu Usman (Birnin Kebbi) and Sukanmi Akanni (Lagos) Nigeria’s much-celebrated rice revolution is facing a major reversal, with more than 90 out of the country’s 260 integrated rice mills shutting down completely over acute paddy scarcity, rising production costs and the influx of cheaper imported rice. This comes as the National Rice Development Strategy II, launched in 2021 to accelerate investments and self sufficiency in rice production expires next month. The programme was part of the Buhari administration’s agricultural transformation agenda, which sought to reduce dependence on food imports and conserve foreign exchange. Nigeria had announced 75 per cent self-sufficiency in rice production in February 2023 and projected to become a net exporter of the commodity by 2026. The progress was showcased in January 2023 when the Federal Government, the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, and Rice Farmers Association of Nigeria, RIFAN, unveiled what they described as the world’s largest rice pyramids in Abuja. The pyramids, comprising one million bags of paddy, were presented as evidence of Nigeria’s growing capacity to produce enough rice for domestic consumption and eventually export the commodity. Nigeria’s annual rice import bill, estimated at about $1 billion in 2015, was said to have fallen to approximately $18.5 million by 2021. But the year 2025 marked the beginning of the reversal of fortune with Paddy production, which had risen to 8.5 million tonnes in 2021, recording a sharp decline to about 4.8 million tonnes, while mill capacity utilisation dropped below 30 per cent. Industry operators told Financial Vanguard that leading integrated mills, including Umza in Kano and Stallion in Lagos, are operating below 50 per cent of their installed capacity. Speaking to the unfolding crisis the National Chairman of the Rice Millers Association of Nigeria, RIMAN, and Chairman, Board of Trustees of the Competitive African Rice Forum for Sustainable Development, CARF-FSD, Nigeria Chapter, Mr. Peter Dama, noted the rice policy inconsistency especially the suspension of the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme (ABP), which drove the country’s rice production surge between 2015 and 2023. The industry operators listed inadequate agricultural financing, insecurity, escalating input costs and weak supply chains as key in the derailing of the growth over the past three years. More recently they said that 2026 has witnessed a deliberate opening of the country’s borders allowing massive importation of cheaper foreign rice especially through Seme border with Benin Republic. item.title: NASA Awards Contract for NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network Program
item.description: Credit: NASA NASA, on behalf of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), has awarded a contract to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation for the Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications (SMBA) instruments on NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network (NEON) satellites. The cost-plus-fixed-fee, firm-fixed-price, and time-and-materials hybrid contract has a value of $290.6 million. The period of performance runs from Nov. 23 through April 1, 2042. The work will take place at the awardee’s facility. Under the contract, Northrop Grumman will provide the design, development, production, testing, and mission support for three SMBA instruments, the next generation of low Earth orbit microwave sounders. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, is managing the acquisition, and NOAA will own and operate the instruments and deliver the data to users worldwide. Microwave sounders provide critical measurements of temperature and moisture in the atmosphere, which significantly influence weather patterns. The SMBA instruments could improve the medium-range forecasts for NOAA’s National Weather Service. The NEON mission is a collaboration between NASA and NOAA. The mission is led by NOAA, which provides funding, technical requirements, and postlaunch operations. NASA will manage the development of the NEON satellites and launch them for NOAA. NASA and NOAA will work with commercial partners to design and build the NEON spacecraft and instruments. item.title: Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC Strive (Nasdaq: ASST) bought no bitcoin last week and sold no stock to fund new purchases, leaving its holdings unchanged at 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday 8-K filing. The Dallas-based company reported that its bitcoin count was unchanged between Nov. 13 and Nov. 20. It sold no Class A common shares, no SATA preferred shares and no SATS preferred shares in its at-the-market programs from the Nov. 13 close through the Nov. 20 close. Strive pauses after two small buys The pause follows a slowdown from the October sprint that built the stack. Strive bought 251 bitcoin for $17.5 million the prior week at an average of $69,853 per coin, after adding just 29 coins the week before that. Bitcoin traded near $61,000 on Coinbase on Monday afternoon. That is about 12.6% below the $69,853 average Strive paid for its most recent purchase. At that price, the 43,404-coin stack is worth roughly $2.65 billion. The filing gives no reason for the pause, and the company has not said whether it plans to resume weekly buying. Strive has typically disclosed its holdings on Mondays, so next week’s update will show whether the stack grows again. Most of the stack was built quickly. Strive held 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 and acquired 15,124 more between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30, including a single 6,182-coin purchase. The company closed a registered offering of 7 million SATS shares on Oct. 20 for about $609 million in net proceeds, which funded much of that run. Cash and preferred holdings Strive’s cash and cash equivalents slipped to $462.4 million as of Nov. 20 from $465.3 million a week earlier, a decline of $2.9 million. The filing does not break out what drove the change. The company also still holds 505,000 shares of Strategy’s variable-rate STRC preferred stock. The fair value of that position fell to $47.3 million from $50.5 million, a drop of about $3.2 million, with the share count unchanged. Share counts were also flat. Strive reported 118,133,002 Class A shares and 9,198,107 Class B shares, for 127,331,109 effective common shares. Outstanding preferred stood at 14,030,176 shares of SATA and 7,141,037 shares of SATS, the 15% perpetual preferred it has used to fund most of its purchases. Strive’s holdings rose from 43,153 bitcoin on Nov. 6 to 43,404 on Nov. 13, and the filing shows no change since. With no common or preferred stock sold, the company raised no new capital through its offering programs last week, which left cash as its main resource for dividends and operations. Shares rally, then fade with the market Strive shares were trading near $15.55 at 3:56 p.m. ET on Monday, up about 7.1% from Friday’s close of $14.51, according to Yahoo Finance. The stock opened near $17.64, a gain of more than 20%, and gave back much of it through the session. item.title: 2027: ‘As You Do For Me, I Do For You,’ Tinubu Seeks Igbo Support In Lagos
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has appealed to Igbo residents in Lagos State to support his re-election bid in the 2027 general elections. President Tinubu made the call while addressing Igbo stakeholders at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, Iganmu, Lagos, on Monday. ﻿ President Tinubu said that though he was displeased when he lost the 2023 election in the state, which is considered a stronghold of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), the matter had been settled. “Some of you didn’t vote for me in 2023; I vex o . We don settle. Get your PVC,” he urged the crowd. Tinubu also asked if they would vote for him, to which they replied with a resounding “Yes.” After receiving assurance from the stakeholders to back his re-election bid, the president said, “Come January 16, get your PVC; you come vote. Agreement na agreement o, na Bola Tinubu be APC o. As you do for me, I do for you.” ‘Follow Who Know Road’ President Tinubu called for national unity and collective responsibility, urging Nigerians to see themselves as one people with a shared future, in the interest of the country. “You must follow who know road. I have to work hard to make sure the economy improves, to ensure that your children are in school, to eliminate crises in the universities, to build good roads that will maintain our cars. “The future is in our hands. For every one of us, our children must be in school. Because we are poor doesn’t mean they shouldn’t attend the universities,” he added. Tinubu further said the country must rise above its divisions, noting that its development depended on the participation and commitment of all its people. Also speaking, the Governor of Lagos State, Mr Babajide Sanwo-Olu, urged Igbo residents to support Tinubu’s re-election and vote for all candidates of the APC in the 2027 general elections. The governor also implored them to work for the emergence of the Deputy Governor and APC governorship candidate, Obafemi Hamzat, as the next Governor of Lagos State. During the meeting, the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi; the Minister of State for Budget and Planning, Doris Uzoka-Anite; and the former Minister of Labour and Employment, Nkiruka Onyejeocha, as well as other Igbo leaders and stakeholders, assured President Tinubu of their support. The Independent National Electoral Commission said Peter Obi, who was the candidate of the Labour Party, polled 582,454 votes in Lagos, higher than the 572,606 votes polled by Tinubu in the February 25, 2023 presidential election. Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial hub, has one of the highest numbers of registered voters for the 2027 general elections. Emphasising the electoral importance of Lagos, Tinubu described it as a big deal to him. ”To me, Lagos is the big deal. How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000-200,000 votes? That’s failure. “Even if you win, and say, ‘A win is a win,’ no. You have to generate the maximum,” he said during a prayer session at the hall of th

item.title: Gov. Mutfwang loses brother
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa Plateau State Governor, Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang, has lost his elder brother, Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang, who died Sunday night following a protracted illness, family sources have disclosed. The Plateau State Government confirmed the death on Monday, as the State Executive Council and the Plateau State Inter-Religious Council paid separate condolence visits to the Governor’s family at the Government House, Jos. The Deputy Governor, Ngo Josephine Piyo, who led members of the State Executive Council on a condolence visit to the Governor’s Residence at the Old Government House, Jos, described the deceased as “a distinguished personality, a devoted family man, a lover of peace and a patriotic Nigerian who made meaningful contributions to public service.” She said the Council received the news of his passing “with profound shock and sadness,” noting that his death was “not only a painful loss to the Mutfwang family but also a significant loss to Plateau State and the nation, given his contributions to society and his exemplary life.” Piyo prayed for the peaceful repose of his soul and asked Almighty God to grant the Governor, the bereaved family and all those mourning his demise “the strength, grace and fortitude to bear the tragic loss.” In a separate visit, the Plateau State Inter-Religious Council also condoled with the Governor and his family over the death of Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang. The delegation, led by the Emir of Wase, Alhaji (Dr.) Muhammadu Sambo Haruna, who spoke on behalf of the Council’s Co-Chairman, Rev. Prof. Pandam Yamsat, described the deceased’s passing as “a painful loss to the family and the state.” Haruna acknowledged the inevitability of death as part of the human experience, urging the bereaved family to “find solace in the sovereignty and wisdom of Almighty God.” He also prayed that God would grant the family “the comfort, strength and resilience needed to navigate this difficult period.” Responding on behalf of the family during the separate condolence visits, Mr. Jonathan Mutfwang expressed “profound appreciation to both delegations for their thoughtful gesture, solidarity and prayers.” He noted that their presence had brought “considerable comfort and encouragement to the bereaved family at this difficult time.” Jonathan also prayed for God’s continued protection, blessings and preservation upon members of the delegations. The family disclosed that the burial of the late Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang has been scheduled for Thursday, November 26, 2026. The condolence visits were disclosed in a statement signed by the Director of Press and Public Affairs to the Governor, Gyang Bere, PhD, and made available to newsmen in Jos on Monday. The post Gov. Mutfwang loses brother appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on Huang’s Return
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on Huang’s Return The bitcoin price slipped back to near $61,100 on Monday afternoon, giving up nearly all of its morning spike even as Wall Street held one of its biggest rallies in years on Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. Bitcoin jumped above $64,000 shortly after the Nvidia news broke before 10 a.m. ET and topped out near $64,500. The move reversed within hours , and the bitcoin price dipped to around $60,800 by 2:45 p.m. ET. It remains up only modestly on the day. The round trip was costly for leveraged traders. Bitcoin liquidations reached about $321 million , with short bets making up $224 million of that total. Liquidations across the broader crypto market topped $762 million. Stocks hold gains as bitcoin fades Stocks kept climbing while bitcoin slid. The Nasdaq Composite was up about 6.9% near 24,170 at about 3:40 p.m. ET, while the S&P 500 gained about 5% and the Dow rose about 3.2%. The S&P 500 had fallen seven straight days before Monday. Nvidia (NVDA) led the move, trading near $165.66, up about 32% from Friday’s close of $125.53. The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, CEO and director, 12 days after he resigned. A stronger dollar may be weighing on the bitcoin price. The dollar index rose about 0.65% to 104.40 , its strongest level since April 2025, as the stock rebound put more Federal Reserve rate hikes back in play. The Fed meets Dec. 8-9, and a quarter-point hike remains the base case. Adam Haeems, head of asset management at Tesseract Group, pointed to steady selling during U.S. market hours since Huang first stepped down. “Bitcoin has fallen in seven of the eight U.S. sessions since Huang went, today’s included, and last week each session’s fall lined up with that day’s ETF outflow,” he said. Crypto stocks keep most of their gains Crypto stocks held up far better than the bitcoin price. Strategy (MSTR) was up about 9.3% near $85.03 in afternoon trading, after it disclosed a purchase of 457 bitcoin last week. Coinbase (COIN) gained about 6.7% to near $108.78, Robinhood (HOOD) rose about 8.8% to near $67.64 and Circle (CRCL) added about 8% to near $51.33. Miners with AI data center businesses posted the biggest moves. IREN (IREN) jumped about 23% to near $14.57, CleanSpark (CLSK) rose about 12.6% and MARA Holdings (MARA) gained about 10%. Core Scientific (CORZ) climbed about 9.4% and Riot Platforms (RIOT) added about 7.1%. ETF flows and inflation data are next Monday’s spot bitcoin ETF flows are the next test. The funds lost about $1.79 billion last week, their fourth straight week of net outflows, as bitcoin slid toward $58,000 on Friday and hit a weekend low near $55,100. “Tonight’s ETF flow figure is the first real test of this bounce,” Haeems said. Strong inflows would suggest buyers are returning, while another round of outflows would raise doubts about how far the rebound can run. Traders also face Wednesday’s inflati

item.title: Delta govt imposes curfew in Ughelli North after campaign rally violence
item.description: The Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area following reported violence at a campaign rally of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Uduere Community, which allegedly left some people dead and several others injured. The curfew, which takes effect from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily, will remain in force until further notice. The Delta State Police Command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bright Edafe. According to the statement, the police have commenced investigations to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible. The Command urged residents to comply strictly with the curfew and cooperate with security personnel to maintain peace and public safety. The statement reads, “The Command therefore urges residents of Ughelli North Local Government Area to comply strictly with the curfew imposed by the Delta State Government, restricting movement between 1800hrs to 0600hrs until further notice. Residents are advised to remain calm and cooperate with security personnel in the interest of public safety. “The Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, CP Samuel E. Erale, psc, mnips, has directed intensified security operations in the affected area to prevent further violence and maintain law and order. The CP has ordered a full-scale investigation and assures residents of the state that anyone found culpable will face the full weight of the law, irrespective of political affiliation or status, and urges members of the public to provide credible information to assist ongoing investigations.” Erale also extended his condolences to the families of those who died and wished the injured a speedy recovery. He reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to protecting lives and property while ensuring a peaceful environment for lawful political activities. The police commissioner further warned political actors and their supporters against thuggery, intimidation and the unlawful use of firearms. He stressed that political differences must never be allowed to degenerate into violence or loss of lives. Vanguard News The post Delta govt imposes curfew in Ughelli North after campaign rally violence appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 89 fall ill after unknown substance released at UK Arena concert
item.description: Thousands of concertgoers were evacuated from the UK’s largest indoor arena after the release of an “unknown substance”, with dozens reporting suffering side effects, police said Monday. Some 12,000 people were attending the Sunday night show by US rapper Don Toliver at the Co-op Live arena in Manchester, northwest England. “A total of 89 people displayed symptoms believed to be linked to exposure,” Manchester police said, adding one woman was taken to hospital for treatment. “Enquiries remain ongoing to establish the nature of the substance, where it came from and any associated risk,” Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said in a statement. Toliver said he had postponed his Monday night London show following the incident, which led to one person being taken to hospital. Emergency services were called after “reports of people in the crowd suffering effects from an unknown substance”, Manchester police said, declaring a major incident at the scene. The venue, which bills itself as the country’s largest live entertainment arena, said it was working with police to “identify the cause of the incident”. The regional ambulance service said it assessed more than 50 people, including some reporting “eye and respiratory symptoms”. Toliver, who was nominated for five Grammy Awards last week, is currently on the second leg of his “Nitrous” world tour. He announced he was rescheduling his show at London’s O2 arena due to an “unfortunate incident last night (in) Manchester”. “My heart and prayers are with everyone that was injured last night,” Toliver said on Instagram, without providing more details. Concertgoers told the BBC that people were “choking” and coughing, recalling “distressing scenes” of people leaving the venue in a panic. Some criticised the lack of security checks at the venue, especially in a city still scarred by the 2017 Manchester Arena bombing, which killed 22 people at an Ariana Grande concert. item.title: Surveillance pricing uses our personal data to make us pay more
item.description: “It costs what it costs” is a mindset I’ve found useful when encountering a sizable, but highly necessary or desired, expense. The sentiment encourages me to accept the price because that’s the accepted value of the gadget, app, or service that I really need or want. But with surveillance pricing, that comfort is no longer a given. I could end up paying more for my TV because of where I am or more for a software subscription because of my age. Surveillance pricing leverages data collected from our web history , smart devices , and apps with the goal of getting us to pay more. That obfuscates the value of products, challenges smart shopping and budgets, and makes it harder for people to get products and services at a fair price. Read full article Comments

item.title: 2027: Armed Men Who Killed Four NDC Campaign Members Said I Was Their Target, Omo-Agege
item.description: Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has alleged that the gunmen who attacked his campaign team in Delta State, killing four people, repeatedly shouted his name and declared their intention to kill him. Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central Senatorial District on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 general elections, said he escaped the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services (DSS) escorts. He spoke on Monday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today . ﻿ Recounting the incident, the former deputy senate president said he heard the attackers repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him while opening fire at the campaign venue. “Right there at the venue, while they were shooting, we could hear them say, ‘It is Omo-Agege we want to kill. We must kill Omo-Agege.’ “But I was lucky because my DSS details were very professional. In fact, after God, the only reason I am alive today is because of the DSS operatives who were with me,” he said. Omo-Agege described the incident as a premeditated attack, alleging that there had been a build-up to the violence. He questioned why he would be singled out for elimination when several other politicians were also contesting elective positions. The former lawmaker said the attackers struck less than five minutes after he began addressing supporters at the campaign venue. According to him, he had moved towards the side of his vehicle to make eye contact with members of the audience when the gunshots rang out. “It was by divine intervention. As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of the vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started,” he said. The former deputy senate president said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others sustained injuries, with some in critical condition. ﻿ In a statement issued earlier on Monday by his media adviser, Sunny Areh, Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation said he survived an assassination attempt during a campaign tour in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. Areh alleged that armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage while he was addressing supporters during a campaign visit. The organisation called for an independent and thorough investigation by the Nigeria Police Force, while appealing to the Inspector-General of Police, the DSS, INEC, civil society organisations and the international community to ensure the safety of political candidates and their supporters. It also urged supporters to remain calm and avoid retaliation, adding that its ward-to-ward campaign activities across Delta Central would continue. item.title: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟
item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. He has since collected four senior caps and added another milestone to his résumé by scoring against Mexico at 17 years and five days old, making him the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.

item.title: Bluetooth brakes are broken as researchers find anyone can control them
item.description: Imagine something as mission-critical as the brakes on a trailer being vulnerable to unauthorized control. One Australian manufacturer made the interesting choice of building Bluetooth into a trailer brake controller without adequately securing its critical braking functions. Anyone within Bluetooth range of an unpatched Elecbrakes trailer controller could potentially trigger its brakes or apply more braking force than intended, without needing to authenticate. The discovery comes courtesy of a pair of security researchers from Element Digital, Patrick Forck and Jeremy McCarthy. Their investigation began earlier this year when Forck was driving down the road and noticed that his physical Elecbrakes In-Car Remote had connected to someone else's trailer without pairing or prompting him. “It had connected mid-drive, without pairing or a prompt, to a brake controller that wasn’t mine, on a trailer I’d never seen, belonging to a driver who had no idea,” the researchers wrote . That one-off connection triggered a full-scale investigation by the pair. For those unfamiliar with trailer brake controllers, these devices are commonly used on larger trailers. Australian manufacturer Elecbrakes sells such controllers in Australia and New Zealand. Depending on jurisdiction, trailers over a certain weight are required to have their own braking system, which Elecbrakes manufactures. Elecbrakes offers two versions that are designed to be easier to install than traditional controllers: One that’s mounted in a vehicle, and one that is mounted directly on a trailer. That trailer-mounted unit can receive Bluetooth commands from the Elecbrakes smartphone app or a separate in-car remote. Given the importance of such control units to road safety, it’s easy to imagine how serious such a vulnerability could be if it proved to be easy to exploit, and boy, did it. Forck and McCarthy admitted they’re infrastructure security guys, not software devs, so they turned to Claude Code to dissect a decompiled copy of the Elecbrakes app, which Claude was happy to oblige. “What came back from the analysis was a map of the device’s entire Bluetooth GATT profile: 47 characteristics across four services, commands sent as plain unencrypted byte arrays, no checksums, no sequence numbers,” the researchers noted. To make matters worse, there was no authentication required for critical braking commands, even though other Bluetooth functions required pairing. Claude then built a web app that ran in Chrome which was able to access the Bluetooth controls for a nearby Elecbrakes system, and they were able to modify practically every aspect of brake control on a unit owned by one of them. Pairing failed on a few attempts, but not where it mattered: It allowed the connection without issue for actual brake control. item.title: Reports: Russia may launch nuclear weapon into orbit as soon as next month
item.description: Western intelligence officials worry that Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite into orbit before the end of the year, suggesting the country's development of a satellite-killing weapon of mass destruction is more advanced than previously thought, German media reported Monday. The orbiting nuclear weapon would threaten thousands of satellites in low-Earth orbit, including military and commercial communications networks like Starshield and Starlink. A nuclear-armed satellite would also put at risk Western military surveillance satellites and human spaceflight platforms like the International Space Station. A nuclear detonation in orbit would be indiscriminate, also knocking out Russia's own spacecraft and Chinese satellites. US lawmakers briefed on government intelligence first disclosed Russia's ambition to deploy a space-based nuclear weapon in early 2024 . At the time, US officials said Russia had launched a test satellite in 2022 to test the effects of radiation on space hardware and pave the way for a future nuclear-armed craft, but that Russia had not yet sent a nuclear weapon into orbit. item.title: How sci‑fi imagines sports in microgravity, and how zero‑g sports might actually work
item.description:
Alan Bradley is an experienced tech and culture writer with more than 20 years covering gaming, tech, and hardware. He has served as commerce director and in senior editorial roles at major publications. His work has appeared in Rolling Stone, U.S. News & World Report, PCMag, TechRadar, GamesRadar+, CNET, Live Science, Variety, and many other outlets. Alan is also a novelist—his debut novel, the urban fantasy The Sixth Borough, is available now.

Sports in space have a long and proud tradition, whether it's Alan Shepard playing golf on the moon or the crew of the ISS hosting their own version of the Summer Olympics . The future looks bright as well, with the foundation of the Space Games Federation , the self-described "first governing and sanctioning body for competitive sports played in zero or micro-gravity," co-founded by a NASA astronaut. Not to be outdone, science fiction has expanded the idea of zero-g and low-gravity sports to their logical extent, imagining everything from Doctor Who's zero-g squash to the advanced, gamified combat simulations of Ender's Game. There was even Space Jam 's alien basketball game for the fate of the planet, though the gravity-defying antics there come from cartoon shenanigans rather than a zero-g playing field. As humanity edges closer to colonizing our neighbors through projects like the Artemis Program and its ambition to establish habitats on the moon, our imaginations have to expand to encompass not only how we'll live in space but also how we'll play. The rules change when gravity disappears (Image credit: Zero-G) We rarely think about it in an Earth context, but every sport is heavily influenced by gravity. It defines how balls arc, how quickly players can move, and even how we orient ourselves in play spaces. Remove the gravity, and all of those assumptions and mechanics evaporate as well. "First of all, in zero g, Isaac Newton will win every time," Les Johnson, former Chief Technologist for NASA, told Space. Les is a physicist with over 35 years of experience working at Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, as well as a science fiction author. "'For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction,'" quotes Johnson. "This is very difficult to simulate in real life due to gravity; special effects often try to compensate. With today’s AI and green screens, it can actually look good on screen." In a microgravity scenario, the concept of up and down is no longer relevant. Suddenly, the playing field expands from a single, fixed plane to a fully three-dimensional space that includes height. (Image credit: Netflix) Momentum is also a completely different beast. Instead of being able to quickly stop and pivot the way you can during terrestrial sports, once you start moving in microgravity, you keep going until something stops you. item.title: Bitdeer Sells All 281 Bitcoin It Mined Last Week, Holds None
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitdeer Sells All 281 Bitcoin It Mined Last Week, Holds None Bitdeer sold every bitcoin it mined last week and still holds none of its own, the company said in its latest weekly update, continuing a nearly year-long strategy of turning production into cash after a weekend plunge in the bitcoin price. The Singapore-based miner reported output of 281.1 BTC and sales of 281.1 BTC for the week, for a net addition of zero. Its pure holdings, which exclude customer deposits, were zero as of Nov. 20. The sales came as bitcoin fell to a weekend low of $55,106 early Saturday at 1:17 AM ET, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows. The price has since bounced to near $62,700 as of 11:23 AM ET Monday. Bitdeer’s reserve has been drained all year Bitdeer’s treasury shrank from roughly 2,000 BTC at the end of 2025 to zero by Feb. 20, when Bitcoin Magazine reported the miner had liquidated its reserve over eight weeks. At the time, the company said the move should not be a concern for the broader market. Bitdeer’s filings show how little it has kept since. In its third-quarter results, filed with the SEC on a Form 6-K on Nov. 10, the company listed 47 BTC held at Sept. 30, down from 2,029 a year earlier. Its September production update showed 61 BTC held at the end of August. The company mined 1,355 BTC in September and 3,855 BTC in the third quarter, compared with 1,109 BTC in the same quarter of 2025. Self-mining margins stay thin Bitdeer has grown its fleet quickly. Self-mining hashrate reached 82.3 exahashes per second in the third quarter, up from 35.0 a year earlier, with another 28.7 exahashes per second of co-mining at third-party sites, the quarterly report shows . The economics are tight. Self-mining generated $217.5 million in revenue in the quarter but only $6.2 million in gross profit. Electricity averaged $47 per megawatt-hour, and the fleet ran at 15.4 joules per terahash. Bitdeer posted record revenue of $320.7 million and adjusted EBITDA of $69.6 million, but a net loss of $125.5 million. That included a $54.6 million non-cash loss tied to a bitcoin-collateralized loan from a related party. Bitdeer also reported $213.7 million in cash and restricted cash, and its board authorized a new $100 million share repurchase program on Oct. 8. Borrowing against coins instead of selling them Not every miner is selling. American Bitcoin secured a $150 million revolving credit line from FalconX on Monday that is backed by its bitcoin. The company said the facility lets it raise cash without drawing down its reserve. The loan carries a 5.95% fee and an initial collateral ratio of 143%. Fully drawing it would require about $214.5 million in pledged bitcoin. American Bitcoin has not said whether it has drawn on the line, and its release lists the risk that pledged coins could be liquidated if prices fall. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 23, 2015: Blue Origin sticks 1st-ever rocket landing from space with its suborbital New Shepard rocket
item.description: null On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing. Before this time, all rockets were single-use only — even SpaceX's rockets. Blue Origin changed the concept forever. After launching the New Shepard capsule safely into space, the rocket started heading back to Earth. It flew towards a landing pad, reignited its engine to slow down and touched down softly on the ground . This was the first successful vertical landing from space in history. The Blue Origin milestone meant that rockets could be reused for multiple missions, which saves money and reduces waste. (Image credit: Blue Origin) Why it mattered Today, SpaceX may be the most well-known for landing its Falcon 9 rocket boosters from orbit. The company's triple-core Falcon Heavy boosters can also land vertically and its massive Starship megarocket can even return to the launch site to be caught by giant metal arms. But in the end, Blue Origin did it first. Blue Origin's New Shepard booster landing kicked off an era of vertical launch and vertical landings for rockets that continues to this day. It may have even outlasted the New Shepard rocket. Since that first landing, Blue Origin has launched 17 suborbital astronaut flights with New Shepard, and 21 more uncrewed flights for a total of 38 missions between April 2015 and 2026. The company reused its New Shepard boosters repeatedly (though it did lose one during an uncrewed launch after a technical issue.) But in January 2026, the company announced a pause in New Shepard flights for two years so that it could focus on moon lander projects. But Blue Origin did not abandon rocket landings. Indeed, the company's success with New Shepard led it to build vertical landing into its larger orbital rocket, New Glenn, which made its first successful landing 2025 — nearly 10 years after that first touchdown. Blue Origin has since reflown a New Glenn booster , and is developing a new rocket engine called Northstar for even better performance. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Critical Cisco remote code execution bug under attack
item.description: Attackers are currently exploiting a critical vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-76466 in Cisco Expressway that allows them to remotely execute commands as root without any authentication, according to warnings from the US government and security researchers. CVE-2026-76466 , which carries a 9.8 CVSS rating, affects Cisco Expressway-C and Cisco Expressway-E gateways configured in clusters, both virtual and physical appliances running vulnerable software. These provide firewall traversal, VPN-less remote access, and call routing for remote users connecting to voice, video, and messaging collaboration services. The bug involves hard-coded authentication credentials and insufficient certificate validation in clustered Expressway deployments. “An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands,” Cisco said in October, when it disclosed the bug and issued a software update that fixed the flaw. “A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying operating system of an affected device.” At the time, the networking vendor said it wasn’t aware of any abuse of the vulnerability. That all changed late last week, however, when Russian security firm F6 said it was investigating “the first observed case” of miscreants exploiting CVE-2026-76466, shortly after a public proof-of-concept exploit became available. “The attackers initially compromised two Cisco Expressway internet-facing devices,” F6’s Cyber Defense Center said on Thursday. “Through one of them, they gained access to two additional cluster nodes located on the organization’s internal network. After obtaining root access, the attackers began preparing tooling for further lateral movement across the infrastructure.” Specifically, the criminals prepared custom Python code to scan the victim’s network and identify files and folders shared over the Server Message Block (SMB) protocol. The scripts were also designed to interact with SQL Server and WinRM, and search GitLab repositories for credentials and other sensitive information. The Python scripts used in the attack indicated that the operator used an AI assistant, according to F6. The security shop also noted that one of the key indicators of compromise is a nodeup “wombat@127.0.0.1” entry in the Erlang system log (erlang.log) on affected Cisco Expressway devices. A day later, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added CVE-2026-76466 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and told federal agencies to patch by Monday. Cisco updated its advisory on Monday to acknowledge CISA’s addition, while noting that it has no direct evidence of active exploitation. The Register reached out to the networking and security vendor for additional details about the scope of the attacks, but did not receive any response. We will update this story as we learn more. ®

item.title: Obi Meets Niger State Residents, Urges Nigerians To Turn Out For 2027 Elections
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians to turn out en masse for the 2027 general elections and remain at their polling units until their votes are counted and transmitted. Obi made the call during a campaign visit to Suleja, Niger State, where he urged voters to resist attempts to manipulate the outcome of the elections by ensuring that their votes were properly accounted for. He also criticised President Bola Tinubu, claiming that the president lacked the physical strength required to govern the country and was more interested in retaining power for personal gains than serving Nigerians. Obi, who is seeking the presidency for the second time, also promised to address Nigeria’s electricity challenges, pledging that his administration would generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000 megawatts of electricity if elected. Niger residents gather for an engagement of NDC Presidential candidate Peter Obi. Photo: NigeriaNDCHQ/X He said Niger State would play a role in achieving the target, citing the state’s resources as part of the potential support for his proposed power-sector plan. The former Anambra State governor has been holding town hall meetings and engaging residents in different states ahead of the 2027 general elections. NDC Presidential candidate Peter Obi. Photo: NigeriaNDCHQ/X Obi contested the 2023 presidential election under the Labour Party, finishing third with 6,101,533 votes, behind Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, who polled 8,794,726 votes, and Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, who received 6,984,520 votes. Tinubu is seeking re-election in 2027, while Obi is contesting under the NDC. Ahead of the election, major contenders include Tinubu under the APC, Atiku of the ADC, and Obi of the NDC. Other parties include the AAC, PDP, APM, SDP, PRP, Labour Party, and YPP. The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections are slated for February 6, 2027. item.title: Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s A solo miner running about 11 terahashes per second has mined Bitcoin block 977,057, collecting a reward of 3.1287 BTC, or about $191,000, on a machine that makes up roughly one-millionth of a percent of the network. The block was found through the solo service at CKpool on Sunday, Nov. 22, at about 7:54 a.m. ET. The reward is the 3.125 BTC subsidy plus about 0.0037 BTC in transaction fees, and it was worth roughly $191,000 at bitcoin’s price when the block landed. How the solo block played out The block holds 584 transactions. Its coinbase transaction pays 3.0661 BTC to a single address and 0.0626 BTC, about 2% of the reward, to a second output. That split matches the service’s 2% fee, which means the miner’s take is a little over $186,000. Con Kolivas, the developer behind CKpool, congratulated the miner on X, whose address he abbreviated as bc1q~zy9j. It matches the end of the address that received the payout. Kolivas called it the 323rd block found on the service and “yet another lucky one.” He said the miner had only about 11.1 TH/s of hashrate on a 3.47 TH worker. “A miner of this size has about a one in 1650 chance of solving a block in a year,” Kolivas wrote. The block was tagged to Solo CK on the mempool.space block explorer, and its coinbase carries the pool’s signature. CKpool describes itself as a service that lets miners go after full solo blocks without running their own node, since you cannot mine directly to a Bitcoin Core node. A recent run of solo wins Solo CK has found five blocks since Nov. 6, according to the explorer’s pool page . The most recent before this one was block 976,642 on Nov. 19, followed by blocks on Nov. 11, Nov. 7 and Nov. 6. Each paid between 3.13 and 3.15 BTC. Earlier this year, a different solo miner won block 943,411 on the same service on April 2, for about 3.139 BTC. In October, a FutureBit Apollo solo miner found block 973,262 and earned 3.154 BTC. Those wins are the exception. Most of the network’s hashrate sits in large pools and industrial operations that split rewards across many miners, which is how they smooth out the luck. A single small machine can run for years without finding anything, and a lucky block can show up on day one. Miners on the service get nothing unless they find a block, and then they keep the full reward minus the 2% fee. Network hashrate and difficulty Bitcoin’s network hashrate was about 1.04 zettahashes per second, or roughly 1,043 exahashes, on a three-day average Monday. At 11.1 TH/s, the winning miner contributes about 0.000001% of that total, which fits Kolivas’s odds. One in 1,650 works out to a chance of about 0.06% over a full year of mining. Mining difficulty is about 134.8 trillion. The last adjustment cut it by about 9.1%, and the next one, expected around Nov. 26, is estimated to raise it by about 9.2%, according to mempool.space. item.title: NASA Seeks Partners to Design First Nuclear Reactor for the Moon
item.description: Artist’s concept of a nuclear fission power system on the Moon’s surface. Credit: NASA NASA is seeking industry partners to develop and test the first nuclear reactor designed to provide electricity on the Moon, a major step toward establishing a sustained human presence on the lunar surface. Lunar Reactor-1 (LR-1) will be a small fission power system that will generate 20 kilowatts of electricity, enough to power approximately 16 average U.S. households annually on Earth. For NASA’s plans for a Moon Base , that energy could support future habitats, communications systems, rovers, scientific instruments, and other essential infrastructure. NASA aims to have a launch-ready system by 2030 and operate it on the Moon for at least five years after deployment. Unlike solar power, which depends on sunlight, a nuclear reactor can generate electricity continuously, including during the Moon’s approximately two-week-long nights. This capability will enable future lunar operations, particularly in locations where sunlight is limited or unavailable. “This request for proposals represents an important step forward as NASA partners with industry to establish an enduring human presence on the lunar surface,” said Brian Giblin, NASA’s Lunar Reactor-1 program manager. “A reliable source of safe and abundant energy will be vital to future exploration of the lunar and Martian surface. Space nuclear systems will provide continuous power to NASA assets in any environment without dependency on sunlight.” NASA’s Space Power and Reactor Capabilities Request for Proposals incorporates feedback received after the agency released a draft proposal in August and hosted an industry day in September at the Ohio Aerospace Institute in Cleveland. The solicitation requires that the reactor must meet Department of Energy (DOE) safety standards for nuclear operations. While the primary purpose of the Request for Proposals is to advance the technology, testing, and flight design of LR-1, NASA may issue additional task orders to support the development of other space nuclear power systems. Proposals are due by Dec. 21. Nuclear power will be increasingly important to NASA’s space exploration ambitions. Lunar nights last about 14 Earth days, while dust storms on Mars can block sunlight for months. Farther from the Sun, solar power becomes progressively less effective. Nuclear systems offer a reliable source of electricity in these challenging environments. LR-1 is managed by the agency’s Space Reactors Division in partnership with the Department of Energy. The division is also responsible for the development of NASA’s Space Reactor‑1 (SR-1) Freedom. Scheduled to launch in 2028, SR-1 Freedom will deliver three SkyFall helicopters to Mars and demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion, which uses electricity generated by a nuclear reactor to power spacecraft propulsion systems. item.title: Bulgaria evicts cyber snoops who lurked inside government networks for 5 years
item.description: The Ancient Thracian heartland of Bulgaria says it has shut down a cyberespionage operation that gave intruders access to government networks for five years – the longest-running known campaign against its administration. Bulgaria's Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation said the unauthorized and officially unattributed attackers first gained access to infrastructure used by government institutions to exchange information in 2021. It explained that the intrusion went unnoticed for so long because "the previous means of protection did not work as a single, integrated system," and that without a new, recently installed product, it may have gone undetected for much longer. "The incident was discovered thanks to the new national cybersecurity system, which for the first time provides a single picture of what is happening in state networks," the ministry added. "Without it, this activity would most likely have remained hidden for an indefinite period of time." Bulgaria acknowledged that "sensitive information related to the work of the state" was accessed, but did not specify the scale of the compromise. Innovation and Digital Transformation Minister Ivan Vasilev said attackers had downloaded more than 130 GB of data over five years. He also put the volume at 62 million pages. The Register contacted the Bulgarian government for confirmation of these numbers. The ministry said that it has not yet found any evidence that citizens' personal data was compromised, and that the affected infrastructure "will be under increased surveillance for 90 days" in case the attackers try to regain access. Vasilev said multiple international hacking groups had accessed government systems since 2021. He did not specify the names of these groups, however, nor did he name any specific countries that may have been involved. In a follow-up interview with bTV , Vasilev blamed political instability and frequent changes of ministerial leadership for leaving government systems inadequately protected. A representative of the Progressive Bulgaria party, which back in May won Bulgaria's eighth general election in five years, Vasilev said the "constant change of leadership" means "important things for the state do not actually happen." Vasilev said the intrusion was discovered over the summer as the national cybersecurity system was upgraded, and that teams had spent the past three to four months removing the attackers. ®

item.title: Weird 'potato chips' and 'ghostly rocks' on Mars spotted by NASA rovers Curiosity and Perseverance
item.description: null NASA's Curiosity and Perseverance rovers have spotted a bizarre assortment of Martian oddities, from potato chip-like rocks and ghostly white formations to mysterious patterns etched into the Red Planet's surface. While their appearances may be unusual, these formations offer scientists something far more valuable than a collection of curious snapshots: clues to the geological processes that shaped Mars over billions of years. In particular, the rocks and mineral deposits could help researchers piece together the planet's watery past and identify environments that may once have been capable of supporting microbial life. NASA's Curiosity rover recently wrapped up a drilling campaign at a location nicknamed "Nazca," where scientists have been examining unusual disk-shaped crystal formations embedded in the surrounding bedrock. Some of the features are so thin and flat that the mission team likened them to potato chips, according to a statement from the space agency. NASA's Curiosity rover captured a close-up view of unusual, disk-shaped crystal formations embedded in Martian bedrock using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI) on Nov. 7, 2026 (Sol 5067). The thin, flattened formations resemble tiny potato chips. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS) Curiosity used its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI), mounted on the end of its robotic arm, to capture detailed close-up images of the formations on Nov. 7 — the rover's 5,067th Martian day , or Sol 5067. The rover also used its ChemCam instrument to study the rocks' chemical composition, while samples from the Nazca drill site were delivered to its onboard Sample Analysis at Mars (SAM) instrument for further analysis. Meanwhile, NASA's Perseverance rover has been investigating a collection of unusually bright rocks in an area called "Idubi," located in the “Lac de Charmes” region outside Jezero Crater. The rover captured images of the formations on Oct. 29, 2026 (Sol 2023), revealing pale, ghostly-looking rocks that stand out dramatically against the darker, dust-covered Martian landscape. Data from Perseverance's SuperCam instrument revealed that the rocks are rich in hydrated silica rather than being typical igneous rocks. That discovery has scientists particularly interested. On Earth, hydrated silica can form in environments involving hydrothermal activity or groundwater. These deposits are also capable of preserving microscopic fossils, making them valuable targets in the search for evidence of ancient life, according to another statement from NASA. NASA's Perseverance rover captured unusually bright, silica-rich rock in the "Idubi" area outside Jezero Crater on Oct. 29, 2026 (Sol 2023), using its left Mastcam-Z camera. The pale formation stands out against the darker, dust-covered Martian terrain. item.title: Microsoft mega outage: Report reveals testing gaps and emails that never arrived
item.description: Some emails never reached their recipients during November's Microsoft 365 outage, the company has confirmed in a final report that also exposes gaps in its testing and recovery procedures. The post-incident report details how a Windows defect brought down Exchange Online and disrupted features across other Microsoft 365 services. For affected users, the cloud became someone else's unavailable computer. A preliminary report had already blamed a July code change, combined with a failover and reduced capacity. The final report confirms those findings and sets out Microsoft's plans to improve change auditing and recovery procedures, and add spare capacity. The defect affected Microsoft's gateway server configuration, not standard Windows deployments. The epic outage (named the "Microsoft long weekend" by some wags) kicked off on November 12 and wasn't fully resolved until November 14. Microsoft extended its delivery retry window to 48 hours, but some delayed messages destined for consumer mailboxes inactive for more than 30 days still expired, generating non-delivery reports. The company said all queued enterprise messages were eventually delivered, with none found permanently lost. The report is grim, particularly in how the failure ramped up as US users came online to find gateway servers toppling over. At the worst point, more than 80 percent of North American gateway servers were unresponsive. The problem proved elusive, and it took Microsoft some time to identify the change and deploy a fix. Microsoft has had a week to ponder what it did and did not do, and the report has some next steps to avoid a repeat of November's events. Some are obvious, and some are a little surprising. Working to reduce the blast radius of failures is an obvious one, and actions include partitioning and isolation to ensure failures can be contained before taking down traffic globally. Recovery procedures also need improvement, along with communication and capacity to ensure there is sufficient headroom. Microsoft's load tests used older, lower-core-count hardware, making them less likely to expose a defect that worsened on newer machines. The company now plans to test newer hardware with more realistic traffic and peak loads, and broaden its failover testing. Microsoft also plans to improve diagnostics and change auditing so engineers can identify troublesome Windows changes faster. July's defect had been running worldwide for more than three months before it brought the gateways down. ®

item.title: Nvidia Soars as Huang Returns, Lifting Stocks and Crypto Shares
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Nvidia Soars as Huang Returns, Lifting Stocks and Crypto Shares Nvidia shares jumped about 35% on Monday after the chipmaker reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO, restoring roughly $1 trillion in market value at the open. The stock traded near $169.20 at 10:41 a.m. ET, up from Friday’s close of $125.53, and Wall Street rallied with it. The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back, effective immediately, after what it called a series of discussions and meetings. It said it received input from “senior levels of the United States government” and is confident his return “poses no national security risk.” President Donald Trump had urged the move. Several items remain open. An independent board committee will finish its investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, and Huang said he will cooperate. Nvidia also formed a national security and export control committee and is searching for a chief compliance officer. From resignation to reversal Huang resigned on Nov. 11, days after admitting an affair with a woman U.S. officials believe is linked to Chinese intelligence. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress became interim CEO and Harvey Jones became board chair. Nvidia had said it was searching for a permanent successor. The stock slid for seven straight weeks, the longest such streak since 2008. On Friday it plunged 14% after Reuters reported that the SEC is examining the company’s accounting practices. Reuters noted that investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing. Huang’s return reverses most of the losses since his affair became public. The selloff came even after Nvidia reported better-than-expected quarterly results on Nov. 17. For weeks, the board had said it was not considering bringing Huang back, which makes Monday’s announcement a sharp turn for the world’s most closely watched chipmaker. Wall Street and chip stocks rally The Nasdaq Composite rose about 7.4% to near 24,300 at 10:41 a.m. ET, and the S&P 500 gained about 5.4% to near 7,280. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed about 3.3%, or more than 1,500 points, to near 49,700. The S&P 500 had fallen seven straight days. Chip stocks followed Nvidia higher. Micron (MU) rose about 21% and Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) gained about 16%, while Intel (INTC) added about 15%. AMD rose about 9% and Broadcom (AVGO) was up about 3%. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned on Sunday that the Fed may be making a “policy mistake” if it overtightens. The central bank meets Dec. 8-9, and a quarter-point increase remains the base case. Bitcoin and crypto stocks follow The bitcoin price climbed to a Monday high near $64,500, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data, and was near $63,000 at 10:41 a.m. ET. That is about $8,000 above the weekend low of $55,106, hit at roughly 1:17 a.m. ET on Saturday. Bitcoin had slid with stocks on Friday. Crypto-linked stocks jumped. item.title: Cross River Bank Launches Its First Bitcoin-Backed Loans With LendingUSA
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Cross River Bank Launches Its First Bitcoin-Backed Loans With LendingUSA Cross River Bank has launched its first bitcoin-backed loans, working with consumer lender LendingUSA to let eligible borrowers take out between $10,000 and $250,000 against their BTC without selling it. The program is the first time Cross River has originated bitcoin-secured loans itself, according to The Block. LendingUSA runs the application platform, and every loan is made by Cross River, a New Jersey state-chartered bank, according to LendingUSA . How the loans work Borrowers can choose a loan-to-value ratio of 30%, 50% or 70%, which sets how much cash they receive against the value of the bitcoin they pledge. LendingUSA defines the ratio as the loan balance divided by the value of the collateral, so a 50% loan against $100,000 of bitcoin would be $50,000. Two repayment options are offered: interest-only or no monthly payments. On an interest-only loan, borrowers make smaller monthly payments that roughly cover interest, with the principal and any remaining interest due at the end of the term. On a no-monthly-payment loan, the full balance plus interest is due at the end. LendingUSA says borrowers can repay early without penalties or fees . Applicants go through a soft credit check, and LendingUSA says approval rests on the crypto being pledged rather than a credit score. The company says funding typically arrives within one to three business days after the collateral is verified. Custody and margin risk A qualified third-party custodian holds the bitcoin for the life of the loan. Once the loan is repaid in full, the collateral is released back to the borrower, according to the company. The terms carry the usual risk of borrowing against a volatile asset. LendingUSA says that if the value of the bitcoin falls, the loan-to-value ratio rises, and borrowers may be asked to add collateral or pay down the debt to avoid liquidation. The company says it will try to notify borrowers first but cannot guarantee it during fast price moves. The timing matters. Bitcoin was trading near $61,000 on Monday morning, so a borrower at the 70% tier would have far less room before a collateral call than one at the 30% tier. Lower ratios leave a bigger cushion but unlock less cash per bitcoin pledged. LendingUSA markets the loans for uses such as debt consolidation, home improvements and large purchases. The company says it has served more than 200,000 borrowers across its lending business, and the crypto product is its first expansion into digital asset-backed loans. A chartered bank joins bitcoin lending Cross River President Evan Russo framed the launch as a natural extension of the bank’s work. “Digital assets have become a meaningful part of how many consumers build and hold wealth, and the financial system must evolve to serve them responsibly,” Russo said in a statement. “Cross River was built on the belief that innovation and trusted infrastructure go hand in hand,”

item.title: 'Avengers: Doomsday' gets final trailer, explaining why Steve Rogers is back and showing an epic battle with the X-Men
item.description: The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday just landed, and it finally puts the spotlight on our boy Steve Rogers. Avengers: Doomsday has been promising the scale and excitement the MCU has often been lacking since the Infinity Saga. Previous trailers played it safe, mostly setting up the conflict and introducing Victor Von Doom. Now it’s time for one last explosive look at the film before it tries to conquer cinemas next month. Disney and Marvel Studios have just released a "final trailer" that puts the focus back on Steve Rogers — no longer Captain America but still ready to use Mjolnir — and Thor as the veterans leading the New Avengers, former colleagues, the Fantastic Four, and even Fox's X-Men (after some first-encounter fights, of course) against Doom and his followers. A few dodgy CG shots aside, it looks grand, and if you're a big X-Men fan, it's hard not to get goosebumps when Cyclops (James Marsden) finally gets to say the thing. The multiverse-spanning story is still largely kept a secret in this trailer, but at least we get a better sense of what the emotional stakes are for Rogers and how all these heroes can realistically work together against the greatest threat they've faced so far (even if most of them won't get more than a few lines). (Image credit: Marvel) As for Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom, this isn't his trailer, but the mysterious Latverian witches — who have fueled many theories online for months — are finally seen in motion. Doom has, however, received a simple but evocative poster that mirrors one of the original Iron Man ones. Even though Marvel Studios' honcho, Kevin Feige, has shot down the theory that this Victor Von Doom is a Tony Stark variant , you can't stop marketing from doing the obvious things, it seems. We won't complain. (Image credit: Marvel Studios) Avengers: Doomsday won't fix all of the Multiverse Saga's shortcomings, but at the very least, it looks like a proper fun time with more toys being mashed together than ever before and proper stakes. Right before Christmas, it's hard to resist such a pitch. Avengers: Doomsday assembles on December 18, 2026, only in cinemas...Yes, it opens the same day as Dune: Part Three . item.title: British retailer Next downplays data breach at tech supplier
item.description: British retailer Next has become the latest high street name to find itself caught up in a cyberattack, although it insists the data accessed by hackers is "benign" and its customers have nothing to worry about. The clothing and homeware giant told investors on Monday that a third-party supplier had suffered a security breach, allowing an unauthorized party to access information relating to Next. The retailer says its own systems remain untouched and that, so far, there's no evidence that customer personal data has fallen into the wrong hands. "We have been informed that one of our third-party online suppliers has experienced a cyber incident which has resulted in unauthorized access to certain benign data relating to NEXT," the company said in its statement, which it shared with The Register . "We took immediate steps to investigate the nature and scope of the incident with the supplier." The breached supplier provides technology services to Next, and the "benign" information accessed is understood to be low-level data. Sensitive customer details, including addresses, passwords, and banking information, are believed to be unaffected. Next hasn't identified the supplier, explained exactly what the hackers managed to get their hands on, or revealed how much information was accessed, and declined to say when asked by The Register . However, the retailer has seemingly decided that the stolen data won’t be of much use to the criminals responsible. "Our investigations are ongoing; however, current evidence indicates that no customer personal data has been compromised," Next said. "The information affected is limited in nature and, based on our current assessment, cannot be used to facilitate fraud against our customers or NEXT." Next also stressed that its own IT infrastructure had escaped unscathed, saying it was "confident that NEXT’s own systems have not been compromised and that this remains an incident affecting the supplier's environment." Despite repeatedly describing the compromised information as harmless, Next says it is treating the incident "with the utmost seriousness" and is working with the affected supplier, law enforcement, and relevant regulators. The incident comes just weeks after fellow British fashion retailer Asos suffered a breach of its own , with hackers gaining access to customer information through third-party platforms. That attack, which came to light on October 6 when customers received an unauthorized push notification through the Asos app announcing that the company had been hacked, was traced to a social engineering scam. An attacker impersonated a trusted contact to trick an Asos employee into handing over login credentials, which were then used to access external platforms. Asos later admitted that the intruders had accessed customer names, contact details, and some account information, but passwords and payment card details were apparently off limits. Credits: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Tea Temim (Columbia), Rick Arendt (UMBC), Dan Milisavljevic (Purdue University); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI) NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has painted a vibrant tapestry of the legendary supernova remnant Cassiopeia A (Cas A). Remnants like these are the clouds of gas and dust that remain following the explosion of a massive star and will eventually seed a new generation of stars and planets. This high-resolution, mid-infrared observation from Webb reveals new details that are helping astronomers chronicle the structure and evolution of Cas A’s original star. The Webb data supports a scenario in which the interior of the star underwent a dramatic change, possibly just hours before its demise. These results published Monday in The Astrophysical Journal Letters . Image: Dust In Cassiopeia A (MIRI Image) NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope reveals the hot dust that makes up Cassiopeia A. The composition of its dust provides clues to the structure of Cassiopeia A’s original star. Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Tea Temim (Columbia University), Rick Arendt (UMBC), Dan Milisavljevic (Purdue University); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI) Stars begin their lives as large clouds of mostly hydrogen gas and cosmic dust called molecular clouds. Eventually, gravity causes these molecular clouds to collapse, the material heats up, and protostars — infant stars — form. Under the constant pressure of gravity, hydrogen within a protostar begins to fuse into helium, which marks the point where protostars evolve into full-fledged stars like our Sun.
